ALL VFR AIRCRAFT OPERATIONS FROM THE SURFACE UP TO BUT NOT INCLUDING FL180, MUST COMPLY WITH THE FOLLOWING DC SFRA SPEED RESTRICTIONS, EXCLUDING FAA-APPROVED DOD, DHS, LAW ENFORCEMENT, AND WAIVERED MEDEVAC/AIR AMBULANCE FLIGHTS: B. IF UNABLE, THE PILOT MUST CONTACT THE APPROPRIATE ATC FACILITY AND ADVISE THEM OF THE AIRCRAFTS OPERATIONAL LIMITATIONS; C. BETWEEN 30NM RADIUS AND 60NM RADIUS OF 385134N0770211W OR THE WASHINGTON DCA VOR/DME, AIRCRAFT MUST MAINTAIN AN AIRSPEED OF 230 KNOTS OR LESS. IF UNABLE, THE PILOT MUST CONTACT THE APPROPRIATE ATC FACILITY AND ADVISE THEM OF THE AIRCRAFTS OPERATIONAL LIMITATIONS PRIOR TO FLYING WITHIN 60NM RADIUS OF THE WASHINGTON DCA VOR/DME; 2409032030-PERM END PART 1 OF 2 FDC 4/9383 ZDC PART 2 OF 2 SECURITY INSTRUCTIONS, WASHINGTON, DC. THIS NOTAM D. SPECIAL AWARENESS TRAINING FOR THE WASHINGTON DC METROPOLITAN AREA IS MANDATORY FOR ALL PILOTS THAT FLY UNDER VFR WITHIN 60NM OF THE DCA VOR/DME (14 CFR PARTS 61 AND 91, EFFECTIVE FEBRUARY 9, 2009). IT IS STRONGLY RECOMMENDED THAT ALL PILOTS FLYING UNDER VISUAL FLIGHT RULES (VFR) WITHIN 100NM OF THE DCA VOR/DME ALSO COMPLETE THIS TRAINING. 2409032030-PERM END PART 2 OF 2

properties.title: NW-C-4475-26 · Routeing Change - North Atlantic Right Whale
properties.rawText:
Effective 241500 UTC Oct 2026, the following North Atlantic Right Whale restriction Zones are in effect for all vessels greater than 13 meters in length overall:
Static Zones North and South: Vessels must not exceed 10 knots over ground.
Dynamic Shipping Zones A, B, C, D, and E: No restriction in effect.
Seasonal Management Areas 1 and 2: No restriction in effect.
Restricted area: No restriction in effect.
Voluntary Seasonal Slowdown: Vessels are requested to reduce their speed less than 10 knots over ground.
Additional details are available in Notices to Mariners. Failure to comply with speed restrictions in effect can lead to enforcement action by Transport Canada.
Mariners are requested to report whale sightings and observations of entangled, dead, or injured whales to Marine Communication and Traffic Services.

properties.title: NW-P-0809-26 · Waterway information - ECHO Program
properties.rawText:
HARO STRAIT AND BOUNDARY PASS – ECHO Program 2025 Voluntary Ship Slowdown
Effective June 15 to November 30, 2026 the ECHO Program voluntary ship slowdown through Haro Strait and Boundary Pass is active for all inbound and outbound commercial and government vessels to reduce underwater noise for at-risk whales. This initiative will remain in effect 24 hours per day until 2359 PDT on November 30, 2026, depending on southern resident killer whale presence in the fall. If it is safe and operationally feasible to do so, commercial and government vessels are requested to not exceed the following speeds through the water:
11 knots – Bulkers, tankers, general cargo vessels, and government vessels; and,
14.5 knots – Vehicle carriers, cruise ships, and container vessels.
This voluntary slowdown takes place between the vessel traffic separation scheme at the south end of Haro Strait at 48-24-22.78 N ,123-12-15.26 W, and the vessel traffic separation scheme at the north end of Boundary Pass at 48-46-39.28 N, 123-1-36.84 W. There are also two optional slow down areas, one rounding Turn Point and the other between Saturna Island and Alden Point, Patos Island.
The ECHO Program is led by the Vancouver Fraser Port Authority in collaboration with government agencies, Indigenous communities, industry partners and environmental groups.
For more detailed information, refer to the following internet web address:
https://www.portvancouver.com/echo/
properties.stationOrArea: Haro Strait, Strait of Georgia, Washington State - San Juan Islands

properties.title: NW-P-0743-26 · Waterway information
properties.rawText:
Effective 0700 UTC JUN 1 2026, to comply with the Interim Order for the Protection of Southern Resident Killer Whales (Orcinus orca) in the Waters of Southern British Columbia, 2026, vessels must not approach within a distance of 1000m of a Southern Resident Killer Whale in the Southern Resident Killer Whale critical habitat and British Columbia coastal waters east of Vancouver Island and south of Campbell River (Cape Mudge) and Ucluelet, including Barkley Sound (up to Port Alberni) and Howe Sound, with coordinates listed in Schedule 1 of the Interim Order.
These prohibitions are in effect until May 31st, 2027. Details of vessel exceptions from the approach distance are described in Sections 2(1), 2(2), 3(2), and 4(2) of the Interim Order. Note that vessels in transit are excepted from the approach distance measure.
Vessels must not operate or navigate within the two Vessel Restricted Zones, specifically those waters off the eastern coast of Saturna Island and southern coast of North Pender Island, with the coordinates listed in Schedule 2 of the Interim Order.
The Vessel Restricted Zones are in effect until November 30th, 2026. Details of vessel exceptions from the Vessel Restricted Zone prohibitions are described in Sections 2(1), 2(2), 5(2) and 6(2) of the Interim Order.
In addition, vessels must adhere to the requirements of two Speed Restricted Zones near Swiftsure Bank, in which all vessels are restricted to a maximum speed of 10 knots over ground, with the coordinates listed in Schedule 3 of the Interim Order.
The Speed Restricted Zones are in effect until November 30th, 2026. Details of vessel exceptions from the Speed Restricted Zones are described in Sections 2(1), 2(2), 7(2) and 8(2) of the Interim Order.
Failure to comply with the Interim Order for the Protection of the Southern Resident Killer Whales in the Waters of Southern British Columbia, 2026 could lead to enforcement action, including fines.
Further details are available at Transport Canada’s website (Interim Order for the Protection of the Southern Resident Killer Whale (Orcinus orca) in the Waters of Southern British Columbia, 2026 (canada.ca), or upon request from a Marine Communications and Traffic Services Centre.

properties.title: NW-C-1839-24 · Waterway information - Calculation of under-keel clearance
properties.rawText:
Canadian Coast Guard Marine Communications and Traffic Services have been using all Canadian Hydrographic Service water-level stations for the calculation of passage authorizations in the SorelMontreal sector of the navigational waterway, namely Sorel, Contrecoeur, Varennes, Montreal-Frontenac and Montreal-Jetty No. 1.
In light of the particular features of the navigational waterway in the portion between buoys M84 (downstream of the municipality of Verchères) and M11 (downstream of the Bellmouth curve), it was agreed to adjust upward the available water column by 10 cm in this portion.
The minimum water column in this portion of the navigational waterway as per the Contrecur hydrographic station, obtained after adjustment, will be used for the calculation of under-keel clearance.

properties.title: NW-C-1838-24 · Waterway information - Calculation of under-keel clearance

In light of the particular features of the navigational waterway in the portion between buoys M84 (downstream of the municipality of Verchères) and M157 (opposite to the Port of Montreal, section 109) as well as the No. 1 Anchorage Pointe-aux-Tremble, it was agreed to adjust upward the available water column by 10 cm in this portion.

Marine Weather Statement issued November 13 at 2:53PM PST by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA

A large west to northwesterly swell is expected to produce
breaking waves at the Morro Bay and Ventura Harbor entrances
on Saturday. These conditions have a history of capsizing vessels
of various sizes resulting in serious injury or death, even to
the most experienced mariners. Mariners are urged to stay clear of
these harbor entrances. For more information, contact the local
harbor patrol or coast guard station...and continue to monitor
NOAA Weather Radio for the latest weather information..

properties.title: Flood Warning
properties.rawText:
Flood Warning issued November 13 at 7:24PM MST until November 17 at 11:00AM MST by NWS Phoenix AZ

* WHAT...Flooding caused by upstream dam release continues.

* WHERE...Maricopa County in south central Arizona...
Northeastern Yuma County in southwestern Arizona...

* WHEN...Until 1100 AM MST Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is expected. Low-water crossings are
likely to become inundated with water and may not be passable.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 724 PM MST, water releases from Painted Rock Dam continue with
flow peaking at 3000 cfs. A streamflow gauge immediately
downstream  also indicated a stage of 9.93 feet.
- Flooding is expected along the Gila River.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Farmlands and low-water crossings along the Gila River.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

properties.title: Flood Warning
properties.rawText:
Flood Warning issued November 13 at 8:40PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL

...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Sanford affecting Seminole County.

.Heavy rainfall has caused river levels on the St. Johns near Sanford
to reach Minor Flood Stage. The river is forecast to remain steady
around Minor Flood Stage into next week.

For the St. Johns River...including Sanford...Minor flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Sanford.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 5.5 feet, Water surrounds homes and covers some
driveways in the Stone Island area near Enterprise in Volusia
County. Water enters yards and floods docks in the River Oaks
Estates subdivision.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:30 PM EST Friday the stage was 5.4 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 4.2 feet.
- Forecast...The river is forecast to remain steady near 5.5 feet
through the weekend and into next week.
- Flood stage is 5.5 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued Saturday afternoon at noon EST.

properties.title: Flood Warning

...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Above Lake Harney affecting Seminole County.

.Heavy rainfall has caused river levels on the St. Johns near Geneva
Above Lake Harney to reach Moderate Flood Stage. River levels are
expected to remain steady into next week.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Above Lake Harney.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

9.1 through the weekend and into next week.

through flooded areas.

properties.title: Flood Warning
properties.rawText:
Flood Warning issued November 13 at 8:29PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL

...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Cocoa 9w affecting Brevard County.

.Recent extreme rainfall over the headwaters of the St. Johns River
has caused the river near Cocoa to rise to Major Flood Stage around
17.1 feet. Additional small rises are possible through the weekend
into next week, before river levels could begin to decline by late
next week.

For the St. Johns River...including Cocoa 9w...Major flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Cocoa 9w.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 17.2 feet, Water enters homes along the St Johns River
in the Lake Poinsett area west of Cocoa, also low lying homes in
the Silver Pines subdivision in Rockledge and the Shakespeare Park
area of Cocoa. Providence Road area west of Cocoa becomes
impassable, cutting off access to homes in the Mullet Lane and Bass
Road area. Docks flooded and water in parking lot at Lone Cabbage
Fish Camp.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:15 PM EST Friday the stage was 17.1 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 15.8 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 7:15 PM EST Friday was 17.1 feet.
- Forecast...The river is forecast to rise to a crest of 17.2 feet
this weekend, hold steady around this level into next week, then
could begin to decline by late next week.
- Flood stage is 16.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued Saturday afternoon at noon EST.

...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Astor affecting Lake and Volusia Counties.

.On the St Johns River at Astor, slight rises within Minor Flood
Stage are forecast this weekend into next week due to a combination
of northerly winds, downstream tidal effects, and water from upstream
heavy rainfall working north through the basin.

For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Minor flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.possible

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 2.8 feet, Docks and boat ramps covered at South Moon
Fish Camp and approaching sea wall at Blair's Jungle Den. Water
approaching sites closest to the river at Fish Tales RV Resort and
Astor Landing Campground. Portion of Clair Street covered by river
water south of the Butler Boat Ramp. Docks underwater at the Astor
Bridge Marina and along Riveredge Drive. Portions of Fox Road are
covered with water nearest to the river. Acorn, Hazelnut and Redbud
roads are underwater with yards inundated.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...

- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 7:30 PM EST Friday was 2.7 feet.
- Forecast...The river is forecast to rise slightly while remaining
in Minor Flood Stage through this weekend and into next week.
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.

properties.title: Flood Warning
properties.rawText:
Flood Warning issued November 14 at 6:40AM MST until November 14 at 9:45AM MST by NWS Salt Lake City UT

* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...West Central Kane County in southern Utah...
Southeastern Washington County in southwestern Utah...

* WHEN...Until 945 AM MST.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of normally dry washes, slot canyons, rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations is
occurring. National Park officials reported all area washes and
streams are running high and fast. The river gauge on the North
Fork of the Virgin River continues to increase, currently near 1000
cfs.  Similarly river gauges on the main stem of the Virgin River
upstream of Quail Creek show flows increasing rapidly.  Gould Wash
in Hurricane is running high.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 636 AM MST, local law enforcement reported heavy rain in the
warned area. Flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Zion National Park, Hurricane, La Verkin, Apple Valley,
Toquerville, Leeds, Virgin, Springdale, Rockville and Pintura.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

properties.title: coastal flooding statement
properties.rawText:
This statement is in effect for parts of the coast due to the following hazard(s): 
- Higher than normal water levels

Elevated ocean water levels are expected with enhanced wave activity and strong winds at times.
 
Hazard: Possible coastal flooding due to storm surge. Water levels will likely exceed highest astronomical tide.
 
When: Today and Sunday. Peak water levels will be observed during high tide, occuring from 11am to 2PM local time.
 
Where:  Low-lying and exposed coastal sections of the Southern Gulf Islands, Saanich Inlet, Swartz Bay to Cordova Bay, Cordova Bay to East Sooke
 
Discussion:
A series of Pacific low-pressure systems are moving across the region and coinciding with a period of high tides this weekend. The storm surge enhancement to the high tide cycle will cause water levels to exceed high astronomical tide. properties.title: Yellow warning · rainfall warning
properties.rawText:
Heavy rain is expected.

Another round of significant rain for the west coast. 

When: This afternoon through Sunday night.

Where: Howe Sound and Sea-to-Sky region.

Remarks:
Another moisture laden low pressure system is heading towards the BC coast. Heavy rain is expected to begin late this afternoon and continue through Sunday.  Total amounts of 40 to 70 mm are possible.

Already saturated ground from a series of storms earlier in the week will lessen the soils ability to absorb moisture, which could intensify the impacts of this round of heavy rain.

Water will likely pool on roads and in low-lying areas. Visibility will likely be suddenly reduced at times.

Watch for washouts near rivers, creeks and culverts.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to BCstorm@ec.gc.ca or post reports on social media using #BCStorm.

properties.title: Yellow warning · blizzard warning
properties.rawText:
Prolonged blizzard conditions with near-zero visibility in blowing snow are expected.

What:
Near-zero visibility in blizzard conditions.

When:
Now through Monday night.

Where:
Dempster Highway near the Richardson Mountains.

Additional information:
A persistent ridge of high pressure over the Beaufort Sea and a low pressure system over the Gulf of Alaska are generating a strong pressure gradient across the Richardson Mountains until Monday night.

Easterly winds of 60 km/h gusting to 80 will further increase to 80 km/h gusting to 110 this morning. Wind-swept snow and falling snow combined with the strong winds will result in blizzard conditions with near-zero visibility. Winds will subside through Sunday, then will strengthen again on Monday. Blizzard conditions will remain.

Road closures are possible.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to YTstorm@ec.gc.ca or post reports on social media using #YTStorm.

properties.title: Flood Warning
properties.rawText:
Flood Warning issued November 14 at 10:14AM EST by NWS Melbourne FL

...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Astor affecting Volusia and Lake Counties.

.On the St Johns River at Astor, slight rises within Minor Flood
Stage are forecast this weekend into next week due to a combination
of northerly winds, downstream tidal effects, and water from upstream
heavy rainfall working north through the basin.

For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Minor flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 3.5 feet, Canals have overflowed into yards. Homes on
or near Wildhog, Bonnet and Snail roads become inaccessible with
several inches of water inside homes along the river and canals.
Docks at Astor Bridge marina and throughout Astor are completely
submerged. Bartram Rd and Holiday Circle are inaccessible with
yards completely submerged. Clair Street is inaccessible. Roads
flooded in South Moon Fish Camp, docks and yards at condominiums on
Juno Trail and water breaches the sea wall at Blair's Jungle Den.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 9:30 AM EST Saturday the stage was 2.6 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 9:30 AM EST Saturday was 2.7 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to 3.4 feet just after
midnight tonight. Additional rises are possible thereafter.
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued Sunday morning at 1130 AM EST.

properties.title: Severe Thunderstorm Warning
properties.rawText:
Severe Thunderstorm Warning issued November 14 at 4:42PM CST until November 14 at 5:30PM CST by NWS Lubbock TX

SVRLUB

The National Weather Service in Lubbock Texas has issued a

* Severe Thunderstorm Warning for...
Northwestern Hockley County in northwestern Texas...
South central Lamb County in northwestern Texas...

* Until 530 PM CST.

* At 442 PM CST, a severe thunderstorm was located 7 miles south of
Pep, or 12 miles east of Morton, moving northeast at 20 mph.

HAZARD...Quarter size hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Damage to vehicles is expected.

* Locations impacted include...
Littlefield and Whitharral.

Remain alert for a possible tornado! Tornadoes can develop quickly
from severe thunderstorms. If you spot a tornado go at once into the
basement or small central room in a sturdy structure.

For your protection move to an interior room on the lowest floor of a
building.

hazardous seas 19 to 21 ft at 16 seconds and south winds 30 to
35 kt with gusts up to 40 kt. For the Storm Warning, seas 17
to 19 ft at 12 seconds and south winds 30 to 40 kt with gusts
up to 45 kt expected. For the second Hazardous Seas Warning,
very steep and hazardous seas 16 to 21 ft at 17 seconds and
south winds 20 to 30 kt expected.

Storm Warning, from 4 PM this afternoon to 4 AM PST Sunday.

could capsize or damage vessels and reduce visibility.

and waves subside.

properties.rawText:
Near-zero visibility in fog continues.

Dense fog has developed over portions of western Saskatchewan.

Conditions are expected to improve later today.

Visibility will likely be suddenly reduced at times.

Fog advisories are issued when widespread poor visibility in fog is expected.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to SKstorm@ec.gc.ca, call 1-800-239-0484 or post reports on social media using #SKStorm.

properties.title: Marine Weather Statement
properties.rawText:
Marine Weather Statement issued November 14 at 3:08PM HST by NWS Honolulu HI

A moderate, long-period north swell from 350 to 360 degrees will
build across Hawaiian waters on Sunday and peak late Sunday and
Monday as the period shortens to 13 seconds. The swell will
produce moderate to heavy surges in north-facing harbors,
especially at Kahului and Hilo Harbors. Mariners using these
harbors should exercise caution when mooring or launching vessels
and when entering or leaving port. The swell will diminish
Tuesday.

properties.title: Flood Warning
properties.rawText:
Flood Warning issued November 14 at 7:02PM CST until November 17 at 12:24AM CST by NWS Corpus Christi TX

...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Texas...

Nueces River Near Tilden affecting McMullen County.

For the Nueces River...including Cotulla, Tilden, Three Rivers,
Mathis, Bluntzer, Calallen...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Nueces River near Tilden.

* WHEN...From this evening to late Monday night.

* IMPACTS...At 15.0 feet, Much of the flood plain below cotulla to
below tilden is cut off, as sloughs and peripheral channels fill.
Hunting cabins, oil field pump jacks and tank batteries flood well
away from the channel. Livestock are cut off and can drown.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 6:30 PM CST Saturday the stage was 13.6 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 11.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage late
this evening to a crest of 14.9 feet Sunday evening. It will then
fall below flood stage Monday.
- Flood stage is 14.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/crp.

properties.title: Flood Warning
properties.rawText:
Flood Warning issued November 14 at 7:51PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL

...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Above Lake Harney affecting Seminole County.

.Heavy rainfall has caused river levels on the St. Johns near Geneva
Above Lake Harney to reach Moderate Flood Stage. River levels are
expected to remain steady into next week.

For the St. Johns River...including Above Lake Harney...Moderate
flooding is forecast.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Above Lake Harney.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 9.0 feet, Water enters the first story of homes on
Whitcomb Drive between Crossover Lane and Lake Harney Road. Water
covers Mullet Lake Park.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:30 PM EST Saturday the stage was 9.0 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 6.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 7:30 PM EST Saturday was 9.1 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to remain steady above flood
stage at 9.0 feet.
- Flood stage is 8.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued Sunday morning at 1100 AM EST.

properties.title: Flood Warning
properties.rawText:
Flood Warning issued November 14 at 7:49PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL

...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Cocoa 9w affecting Brevard County.

.Recent extreme rainfall over the headwaters of the St. Johns River
has caused the river near Cocoa to rise to Major Flood Stage. The
river is forecast to continue remain steady with slight deviations in
river levels through at least early next week.

For the St. Johns River...including Cocoa 9w...Major flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Cocoa 9w.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 17.2 feet, Water enters homes along the St Johns River
in the Lake Poinsett area west of Cocoa, also low lying homes in
the Silver Pines subdivision in Rockledge and the Shakespeare Park
area of Cocoa. Providence Road area west of Cocoa becomes
impassable, cutting off access to homes in the Mullet Lane and Bass
Road area. Docks flooded and water in parking lot at Lone Cabbage
Fish Camp.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:15 PM EST Saturday the stage was 17.0 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 15.8 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 7:15 PM EST Saturday was 17.1 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 17.1 feet
just after midnight tonight.

properties.title: Flood Warning
properties.rawText:
Flood Warning issued November 14 at 7:47PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL

...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Astor affecting Lake and Volusia Counties.

.On the St Johns River at Astor, slight rises within Minor Flood
Stage are forecast early next week due to a combination of northerly
winds, downstream tidal effects, and water from upstream heavy
rainfall working north through the basin.

For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Minor flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 2.8 feet, Docks and boat ramps covered at South Moon
Fish Camp and approaching sea wall at Blair's Jungle Den. Water
approaching sites closest to the river at Fish Tales RV Resort and
Astor Landing Campground. Portion of Clair Street covered by river
water south of the Butler Boat Ramp. Docks underwater at the Astor
Bridge Marina and along Riveredge Drive. Portions of Fox Road are
covered with water nearest to the river. Acorn, Hazelnut and Redbud
roads are underwater with yards inundated.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 6:30 PM EST Saturday the stage was 2.6 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 6:30 PM EST Saturday was 2.7 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to remain steady above flood
stage at 2.6 feet.
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued Sunday morning at 1100 AM EST.

properties.title: coastal flooding statement
properties.rawText:
This statement is in effect for parts of the coast due to the following hazard(s): 
- Higher than normal water levels

Elevated ocean water levels are expected with enhanced wave activity and strong winds at times.
 
Hazard: Possible coastal flooding due to storm surge. Water levels will likely exceed highest astronomical tide.
 
When: Sunday. Peak water levels will be observed during high tide, occuring from 11am to 2PM local time.
 
Where:  Low-lying and exposed coastal sections of the Southern Gulf Islands, Saanich Inlet, Swartz Bay to Cordova Bay, Cordova Bay to East Sooke
 
Discussion:
A series of Pacific low-pressure systems are moving across the region and coinciding with a period of high tides this weekend. The storm surge enhancement to the high tide cycle will cause water levels to exceed high astronomical tide.  East to southeasterly winds gusting from 60 to 90 km/h  are expected over exposed coastal sections tonight and will cause enhanced wave action and swells in some areas.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to BCstorm@ec.gc.ca or post reports on social media using #BCStorm.
properties.stationOrArea: Shoreline of Saanich Inlet; Greater Victoria Coastline: Swartz Bay to Cordova Bay; Greater Victoria Coastline: Cordova Bay to East Sooke and 1 more areas

properties.title: Yellow warning · wind warning
properties.rawText:
Another strong wind event is expected over coastal B.C.

What: Southeasterly winds of 90 km/h gusting to 110 km/h.

Where: Coastal sections of West Vancouver Island, North Vancouver Island, and Haida Gwaii.

When: 
- This evening for Vancouver Island. 
- Tonight and Sunday for Haida Gwaii.

Remarks:  Very strong winds with gusts up to 110 km/h will persist over the BC Coast this evening before easing below warning criteria overnight. Haida Gwaii will see a second push of strong winds midday on Sunday.

Local utility outages are possible. Disruptions to services and travel are possible.

Secure loose objects.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to BCstorm@ec.gc.ca or post reports on social media using #BCStorm.

properties.title: Yellow warning · wind warning
properties.rawText:
Another strong wind event is expected over coastal B.C.

What: Southeasterly winds of 70 km/h gusting to 90 km/h.

When: Late this evening to early Sunday morning.

Where: Exposed coasts along the Strait of Georgia.

Remarks:
A vigorous frontal system moving across the South Coast tonight will bring strong southeast winds to the region. For exposed areas along the Strait of Georgia, southeast winds will gradually strengthen this evening and reach 70 km/h gusting to 90 km/h near midnight. 

Strong winds will ease below warning criteria early Sunday morning in the wake of the system.

Local utility outages are possible.

Secure loose objects. Be prepared to adapt your driving for changing conditions.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to BCstorm@ec.gc.ca or post reports on social media using #BCStorm.

properties.title: Yellow warning · rainfall warning
properties.rawText:
Heavy rain is expected.

Another round of significant rain for the west coast. 

When: Now through Sunday night.

Where: West Vancouver Island, Inland Vancouver Island & North Vancouver Island.

Remarks:
Another moisture laden low pressure system will move across the South Coast and bring prolonged periods of rain to the region. Rain will intensify this evening and change to periods of moderate rain Sunday afternoon before easing to light showers Sunday overnight. 

Total rainfall amounts over the region extending between Zeballos, Gold River and Port Alice is expected to reach between 80 to 150 mm, while Tofino and locations further south can expect between 50 to 100 mm.

Water will likely pool on roads and in low-lying areas.

Watch for washouts near rivers, creeks and culverts.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to BCstorm@ec.gc.ca or post reports on social media using #BCStorm.
properties.stationOrArea: North Vancouver Island; West Vancouver Island; Inland Vancouver Island

properties.title: Yellow warning · rainfall warning
properties.rawText:
Another round of significant rain for the west coast. 

When: This evening to Sunday evening.

Where: Howe Sound and Sea-to-Sky region.

Remarks:
Another moisture laden low pressure system will move across the South Coast tonight. Heavy rain is expected to begin this evening and ease to light to moderate showers Sunday evening. Total rainfall amounts of 40 to 70 mm are possible.

Already saturated ground from a series of storms earlier in the week will lessen the soil's ability to absorb moisture, which could intensify the impacts of this round of heavy rain.

Water will likely pool on roads and in low-lying areas. Visibility will likely be suddenly reduced at times.

Watch for washouts near rivers, creeks and culverts.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to BCstorm@ec.gc.ca or post reports on social media using #BCStorm.

properties.title: Yellow warning · blizzard warning
properties.rawText:
Prolonged blizzard conditions with near-zero visibility in blowing snow are expected.

What:
Near-zero visibility in blizzard conditions.

When:
Now through Monday night.

Where:
Dempster Highway near the Richardson Mountains.

Additional information:
A persistent ridge of high pressure over the Beaufort Sea and a low pressure system over the Gulf of Alaska are generating a strong pressure gradient across the Richardson Mountains that will ease somewhat overnight and strengthen again on Monday.

Easterly winds of 90 km/h gusting to 110 will ease overnight and then increase early Monday morning. Wind-swept snow and falling snow combined with the strong winds will result in blizzard conditions with near-zero visibility. Blizzard conditions will remain.

Road closures are possible.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to YTstorm@ec.gc.ca or post reports on social media using #YTStorm.

properties.rawText:
Gale Warning issued November 15 at 1:37AM PST until November 15 at 7:00AM PST by NWS Seattle WA

* WHAT...For the Gale Warning, southeast winds 25 to 35 kt. For
the Small Craft Advisory, south winds 15 to 25 kt.

* WHERE...East Entrance U. S. Waters Strait Of Juan De Fuca.

* WHEN...For the Gale Warning, until 7 AM PST this morning. For
the Small Craft Advisory, from 7 AM this morning to 4 AM PST
Monday.

* IMPACTS...Strong winds will cause hazardous seas which could
capsize or damage vessels and reduce visibility.

A Gale Warning means winds of 34 to 47 knots are imminent or
occurring. Operating a vessel in gale conditions requires
experience and properly equipped vessels. It is highly
recommended that mariners without the proper experience seek safe
harbor prior to the onset of gale conditions.

properties.title: Special Marine Warning
properties.rawText:
Special Marine Warning issued November 15 at 2:57AM CST until November 15 at 4:00AM CST by NWS Corpus Christi TX

SMWCRP

The National Weather Service in Corpus Christi has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
Waters from Port Aransas to Matagorda Ship Channel from 20 to 60
NM...

* Until 400 AM CST.

* At 257 AM CST, a severe thunderstorm capable of producing
waterspouts was located 44 NM south of Port Oconnor, moving east at
10 knots.

HAZARD...Waterspouts and wind gusts to 40 knots.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Waterspouts can easily overturn boats and create locally
hazardous seas. Small craft could be damaged in briefly
higher winds and suddenly higher waves.

* Locations impacted include...
Mainly open waters from Port Aransas to Matagorda Ship Channel from
20 to 60 NM.

Move to safe harbor until hazardous weather passes.

properties.title: Flood Warning
properties.rawText:
Flood Warning issued November 14 at 9:58PM PST until November 16 at 1:00PM PST by NWS Seattle WA

...The National Weather Service in Seattle has issued a Flood Warning
for the following rivers in Washington...

Skokomish River At Potlatch affecting Mason County.

.Heavy rain along the south slopes of the Olympics overnight will
push the Skokomish River above flood stage Sunday morning.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Skokomish River at Potlatch.

* WHEN...From late tonight to Monday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...At 16.5 feet, the Skokomish River will cause widespread
flooding of pasture lands, with water flowing quickly over West
Bourgault Road and Skokomish Valley Road.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 9:30 PM PST Saturday the stage was 16.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage late
tonight to a crest of 17.1 feet late Sunday morning. It will then
fall below flood stage early Monday morning.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued Sunday morning at 630 AM PST.

properties.title: coastal flooding statement
properties.rawText:
This statement is in effect for parts of the coast due to the following hazard(s): 
- Higher than normal water levels

Elevated ocean water levels are expected with enhanced wave activity and strong winds at times.
 
Hazard: Possible coastal flooding due to storm surge. Water levels will likely exceed highest astronomical tide.
 
When: During Sunday high tide, occuring from 11am to 2PM local time.
 
Where:  Low-lying and exposed coastal sections of the Southern Gulf Islands, Saanich Inlet, Swartz Bay to Cordova Bay, Cordova Bay to East Sooke
 
Discussion:
A series of Pacific low-pressure systems are moving across the region and coinciding with a period of high tides this weekend. The storm surge enhancement to the high tide cycle will cause water levels to exceed high astronomical tide.  East to southeasterly winds gusting from 60 to 90 km/h  are expected over exposed coastal sections tonight and will cause enhanced wave action and swells in some areas.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to BCstorm@ec.gc.ca or post reports on social media using #BCStorm.

Dense fog is expected or occurring.

There is also risk of freezing drizzle.

Conditions will slowly improve Sunday morning.

Visibility will likely be suddenly reduced at times.

Be prepared for areas of near-zero visibility and allow extra time to reach your destination. If driving, turn on your lights, slow down and maintain a safe following distance.

properties.title: Yellow warning · rainfall warning
properties.rawText:
Heavy rain is expected.

When: Now to Sunday morning.

Where: East Vancouver Island - Courtenay to Campbell River.

Remarks:
Another moisture laden low pressure system is moving across the South Coast tonight. Rain will intensify this evening and ease Sunday morning with total rainfall amounts near 50 mm .

Water will likely pool on roads and in low-lying areas. Visibility will likely be suddenly reduced at times.

Watch for washouts near rivers, creeks and culverts.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to BCstorm@ec.gc.ca or post reports on social media using #BCStorm.

properties.title: Yellow warning · rainfall warning
properties.rawText:
Another round of significant rain for the west coast. 

When: Now to Sunday evening.

Where: Howe Sound and Sea-to-Sky region.

Remarks:
Another moisture laden low pressure system is moving across the South Coast tonight. Heavy rain tonight will ease to light to moderate showers Sunday evening. Total rainfall amounts of 40 to 70 mm are possible.

Already saturated ground from a series of storms earlier in the week will lessen the soil's ability to absorb moisture, which could intensify the impacts of this round of heavy rain.

Water will likely pool on roads and in low-lying areas. Visibility will likely be suddenly reduced at times.

Watch for washouts near rivers, creeks and culverts.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to BCstorm@ec.gc.ca or post reports on social media using #BCStorm.

immediately until this storm passes.

properties.title: Marine Weather Statement
properties.rawText:
Marine Weather Statement issued November 15 at 3:26AM PST by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA

A large west to northwesterly swell will continue to produce
breaking waves at the Morro Bay and Ventura Harbor entrances
through at least this afternoon. These conditions have a history
of capsizing vessels of various sizes resulting in serious injury
or death, even to the most experienced mariners. Mariners are
urged to stay clear of these harbor entrances. For more
information, contact the local harbor patrol or coast guard
station and continue to monitor NOAA Weather Radio for the latest
weather information.

extremely rough bay waters.

Small Craft Advisory, from 6 AM to 3 PM CST Monday.

vessel for hazardous conditions.

properties.title: coastal flooding statement
properties.rawText:
This statement is in effect for parts of the coast due to the following hazard(s): 
- Higher than normal water levels

Elevated ocean water levels are expected with enhanced wave activity and strong winds at times.
 
Hazard: Possible coastal flooding due to storm surge. Water levels will likely exceed highest astronomical tide.
 
When: Today. Peak water levels will be observed during high tide, occcurring from 10AM to 12PM local time.
 
Where: Low-lying and exposed coastal sections of Metro Vancouver and Musqueam First Nation including Boundary Bay to Semiahmoo Bay.

Discussion:
A series of Pacific low-pressure systems are moving across the region this weekend and coinciding with a period of high tides. High tides are likely to surpass predicted levels due to storm surge enhancement. East to southeasterly winds gusting 60-80 km/h this weekend are expected over exposed coastal sections at times, and will cause enhanced wave action and swells in some areas.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to BCstorm@ec.gc.ca or post reports on social media using #BCStorm.
properties.stationOrArea: Shoreline of the Strait of Georgia including Tsawwassen; Boundary Bay including Beach Grove; Mud and Semiahmoo Bay: South Surrey - White Rock - Semiahmoo FN and 1 more areas

properties.title: Yellow warning · rainfall warning
properties.rawText:
Another period of rain for the west coast. 

When: Today.

Where: Howe Sound and Sea-to-Sky region.

Remarks:
Another moisture laden low pressure system is moving across the South Coast today. Rain will ease to light to moderate showers this evening. Total rainfall amounts of 40 to 70 mm are possible.

Already saturated ground from a series of storms earlier in the week will lessen the soil's ability to absorb moisture, which could intensify the impacts of this round of heavy rain.

Water will likely pool on roads and in low-lying areas. Visibility will likely be suddenly reduced at times.

Watch for washouts near rivers, creeks and culverts.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to BCstorm@ec.gc.ca or post reports on social media using #BCStorm.

properties.title: Yellow warning · rainfall warning
properties.rawText:
Heavy rain is expected.

Another round of significant rain for the west coast. 

When: Today and tonight.

Where: West Vancouver Island, Inland Vancouver Island & North Vancouver Island.

Remarks:
Another moisture laden low pressure system is crossing the South Coast and bring prolonged periods of rain to the region today. Heayv rain will change to periods of moderate rain this afternoon before easing to light showers overnight. 

Total rainfall amounts over the region extending between Zeballos, Gold River and Port Alice is expected to reach between 80 to 150 mm, while Tofino and locations further south can expect between 50 to 100 mm.

Water will likely pool on roads and in low-lying areas.

properties.title: Yellow warning · rainfall warning
properties.rawText:
Heavy rain is expected.

When: This morning.

Where: East Vancouver Island - Courtenay to Campbell River.

Remarks:
Another moisture laden low pressure system is moving across the South Coast. Rain will ease this morning, with total rainfall amounts near 50 mm .

Water will likely pool on roads and in low-lying areas. Visibility will likely be suddenly reduced at times.

Watch for washouts near rivers, creeks and culverts.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to BCstorm@ec.gc.ca or post reports on social media using #BCStorm.

properties.title: Yellow warning · blizzard warning
properties.rawText:
Prolonged blizzard conditions with near-zero visibility in blowing snow are expected.

What:
Near-zero visibility in blizzard conditions.

When:
Monday.

Where:
Dempster Highway near the Richardson Mountains.

Additional information:
A persistent ridge of high pressure over the Beaufort Sea and a low pressure system over the Gulf of Alaska are generating a strong pressure gradient across the Richardson Mountains that will strengthen again on Monday.

Easterly winds will re-develop early Monday morning and increase to gusting to 100 km/h on Monday evening. Wind-swept snow and falling snow combined with the strong winds will result in blizzard conditions with near-zero visibility.

Road closures are possible.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to YTstorm@ec.gc.ca or post reports on social media using #YTStorm.

properties.title: Hazardous Seas Warning
properties.rawText:
Hazardous Seas Warning issued November 15 at 12:24PM PST until November 16 at 7:00PM PST by NWS Portland OR

* WHAT...Very steep and hazardous seas 16 to 21 ft at 16 seconds
and south winds 10 to 20 kt with gusts up to 25 kt.

* WHERE...In the Main Channel of the Columbia River Bar.

* WHEN...Until 7 PM PST Monday.

* IMPACTS...Very steep and hazardous seas could capsize or cause
damage to vessels.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS... First Ebb current of 4.04 kt at 806 PM
Sunday. Seas 19 to 21 ft. Second Ebb current of 2.12 kt at 927
AM Monday. Seas 16 to 18 ft. Third Ebb current of 3.62 kt at 904
PM Monday. Seas 12 to 14 ft.

A Hazardous Seas Warning means hazardous sea conditions are
imminent or occurring. Recreational boaters should remain in
port, or take shelter until waves subside.  Commercial vessels
should prepare for rough seas and consider remaining in port or
taking shelter in port until hazardous seas subside.

* WHAT...South to southwest winds 15 to 25 kt with very steep and
hazardous swell dominated seas 17 to 22 ft at 16 seconds. Swell

damage vessels. Low visibility conditions are possible.

very steep seas. Remain in port, seek safe harbor, alter course,
and/or secure the vessel for severe conditions.

properties.title: Flood Warning
properties.rawText:
Flood Warning issued November 15 at 1:30PM CST until November 18 at 1:45AM CST by NWS Corpus Christi TX

...Forecast flooding changed from Minor to Moderate severity and
increased in duration for the following rivers in Texas...

Nueces River Near Tilden affecting McMullen County.

For the Nueces River...including Tilden...Moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...Nueces River near Tilden.

* WHEN...Until late Tuesday night.

* IMPACTS...At 16.0 feet, Moderate lowland flooding occurs. Hunting
cabins, oil field tanks and pumps are affected, and livestock
become isolated.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 12:30 PM CST Sunday the stage was 16.0 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 11.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 16.2 feet
this evening. It will then fall below flood stage late Tuesday
morning.
- Flood stage is 14.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/crp.

properties.title: Special Marine Warning
properties.rawText:
Special Marine Warning issued November 15 at 6:50PM CST until November 15 at 8:15PM CST by NWS Houston/Galveston TX

SMWHGX

The National Weather Service in League City has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
Waters from Freeport to Matagorda Ship Channel TX from 20 to 60
NM...
Waters from High Island to Freeport TX from 20 to 60 NM...

* Until 815 PM CST.

* At 648 PM CST, a line of severe thunderstorms capable of producing
waterspouts was located 40 NM off the Upper Texas Coast, moving
southeast at 30 knots.

HAZARD...Waterspouts and wind gusts to nearly 50 knots.

SOURCE...Radar.

IMPACT...Waterspouts can easily overturn boats and create locally
hazardous seas. Small craft could be damaged in briefly
higher winds and suddenly higher waves.

* Locations impacted include...
Galveston A122, Galveston A196, Galveston A250, Galveston A171,
Brazos A85, High Island A457, Buoy 42019, High Island A142, High
Island A131, High Island A410, Brazos A110, East Breaks 228,
Galveston A156, and Galveston A66.

Move to safe harbor until hazardous weather passes.

Move to safe harbor immediately as gusty winds and high waves are
expected.

Thunderstorms can produce sudden waterspouts. Waterspouts can easily
overturn boats and create locally hazardous seas. Seek safe harbor
immediately.
properties.stationOrArea: Waters from Freeport to Matagorda Ship Channel TX from 20 to 60 NM; Waters from High Island to Freeport TX from 20 to 60 NM

properties.title: Flood Warning
properties.rawText:
Flood Warning issued November 15 at 7:43PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL

...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Astor affecting Volusia and Lake Counties.

.On the St Johns River at Astor, slight rises within Minor Flood
Stage are forecast through at least midweek due to a combination of
northerly winds and water from upstream heavy rainfall working north
through the basin.

For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Minor flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 2.8 feet, Docks and boat ramps covered at South Moon
Fish Camp and approaching sea wall at Blair's Jungle Den. Water
approaching sites closest to the river at Fish Tales RV Resort and
Astor Landing Campground. Portion of Clair Street covered by river
water south of the Butler Boat Ramp. Docks underwater at the Astor
Bridge Marina and along Riveredge Drive. Portions of Fox Road are
covered with water nearest to the river. Acorn, Hazelnut and Redbud
roads are underwater with yards inundated.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 6:30 PM EST Sunday the stage was 2.6 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 6:30 PM EST Sunday was 2.6 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to remain steady above flood
stage at 2.6 feet.
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued Monday morning at 1100 AM EST.

properties.title: Flood Warning
properties.rawText:
Flood Warning issued November 15 at 7:41PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL

...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Cocoa 9w affecting Brevard County.

.Recent extreme rainfall over the headwaters of the St. Johns River
has caused the river near Cocoa to rise to Major Flood Stage. The
river is forecast to continue to remain steady with slight deviations
in river levels through at least midweek.

For the St. Johns River...including Cocoa 9w...Major flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Cocoa 9w.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 17.2 feet, Water enters homes along the St Johns River
in the Lake Poinsett area west of Cocoa, also low lying homes in
the Silver Pines subdivision in Rockledge and the Shakespeare Park
area of Cocoa. Providence Road area west of Cocoa becomes
impassable, cutting off access to homes in the Mullet Lane and Bass
Road area. Docks flooded and water in parking lot at Lone Cabbage
Fish Camp.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:15 PM EST Sunday the stage was 17.1 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 15.8 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 7:15 PM EST Sunday was 17.1 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 17.1 feet
just after midnight tonight.

through flooded areas.

Marine Weather Statement issued November 15 at 6:34PM CST by NWS Brownsville TX

The areas affected include...
Coastal waters from Baffin Bay to Port Mansfield TX out 20 NM...
Coastal waters from Port Mansfield TX to the Rio Grande River out
20 NM...
Laguna Madre From 5 nm North Of Port Mansfield To Baffin Bay TX...
Laguna Madre From The Arroyo Colorado To 5 NM North Of Port
Mansfield TX...
Laguna Madre From the Port Of Brownsville to the Arroyo
Colorado...
Waters from Port Mansfield TX to the Rio Grande River from 20 to
60 NM...

At 634 PM CST, Doppler radar indicated strong thunderstorms, capable
of producing winds to around 30 knots. These thunderstorms were
located along a line extending from 19 nm east of Laguna Madre to 7
nm southeast of Port Mansfield, moving south at 15 knots.

Mariners can expect gusty winds to around 30 knots, locally higher
waves, and lightning strikes. Boaters should seek safe harbor
immediately until these storms pass.

properties.title: Flood Warning
properties.rawText:
Flood Warning issued November 15 at 1:55PM PST until November 16 at 11:53AM PST by NWS Seattle WA

...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in
Washington...

Skokomish River At Potlatch affecting Mason County.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Skokomish River at Potlatch.

* WHEN...Until Monday morning.

* IMPACTS...At 16.5 feet, the Skokomish River will cause widespread
flooding of pasture lands, with water flowing quickly over West
Bourgault Road and Skokomish Valley Road.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1:30 PM PST Sunday the stage was 17.1 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 1:30 PM PST Sunday was 17.2 feet.
- Forecast...The river has crested and is expected to fall below
flood stage tonight and continue to recede on Monday.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued this evening at 1000 PM PST.

properties.title: Yellow advisory · fog advisory
properties.rawText:
Near-zero visibility in fog continues over some areas.

While some areas may see conditions improve tonight, fog may persist into Monday morning in some places.

Visibility will likely be suddenly reduced at times.

Be prepared for areas of near-zero visibility and allow extra time to reach your destination. If driving, turn on your lights, slow down and maintain a safe following distance.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to ABstorm@ec.gc.ca, call 1-800-239-0484 or post reports on social media using #ABStorm.

properties.title: Yellow warning · rainfall warning
properties.rawText:
Periods of rain continues. 

When: Now to this evening.

Where: Howe Sound and Sea-to-Sky region.

Remarks:
A moisture laden low pressure system brought heavy rain to the region Saturday night. In the wake of the system, periods of rain will continue today and ease to light showers this evening. Total rainfall amounts near 40 are possible.

Already saturated ground from a series of storms earlier in the week will lessen the soil's ability to absorb moisture, which could intensify the impacts of this round of heavy rain.

Water will likely pool on roads and in low-lying areas. Visibility will likely be suddenly reduced at times.

Watch for washouts near rivers, creeks and culverts.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to BCstorm@ec.gc.ca or post reports on social media using #BCStorm.

properties.title: Yellow warning · blizzard warning
properties.rawText:
Prolonged blizzard conditions with near-zero visibility in blowing snow are expected.

What:
Near-zero visibility in blizzard conditions.

When:
Monday.

Where:
Dempster Highway near the Richardson Mountains.

Additional information:
A persistent ridge of high pressure over the Beaufort Sea and a low pressure system over the Gulf of Alaska are generating a strong pressure gradient across the Richardson Mountains that will strengthen again on Monday.

Easterly winds will re-develop early Monday morning and increase to gusting to 100 km/h on Monday evening. Wind-swept snow and falling snow combined with the strong winds will result in blizzard conditions with near-zero visibility.

Road closures are possible.

If driving, turn on your lights, slow down and maintain a safe following distance.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to YTstorm@ec.gc.ca or post reports on social media using #YTStorm.

properties.title: Flood Warning
properties.rawText:
Flood Warning issued November 15 at 9:54PM PST until November 16 at 11:53AM PST by NWS Seattle WA

...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in
Washington...

Skokomish River At Potlatch affecting Mason County.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Skokomish River at Potlatch.

* WHEN...Until Monday morning.

* IMPACTS...At 16.5 feet, the Skokomish River will cause widespread
flooding of pasture lands, with water flowing quickly over West
Bourgault Road and Skokomish Valley Road.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 9:30 PM PST Sunday the stage was 16.7 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 9:30 PM PST Sunday was 17.2 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to fall below flood stage early
Monday morning and remain below flood stage through the week.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued Monday morning at 600 AM PST.

properties.title: Hazardous Seas Warning
properties.rawText:
Hazardous Seas Warning issued November 15 at 8:30PM PST until November 16 at 3:00PM PST by NWS Eureka CA

* WHAT...For the Hazardous Seas Warning, very steep and
hazardous seas 17 to 19 feet. For the Gale Watch, south winds
25 to 35 kt with gusts up to 50 kt and seas 10 to 13 feet
possible.

* WHERE...Waters from Cape Mendocino to Pt. Arena CA from 10 to
60 nm.

* WHEN...For the Hazardous Seas Warning, until 3 PM PST Monday.
For the Gale Watch, from Tuesday afternoon through late
Tuesday night.

* IMPACTS...Strong winds can cause hazardous seas which could
capsize or damage vessels and reduce visibility.

Mariners should consider altering plans to avoid possible
hazardous conditions.  Remain in port, seek safe harbor, alter
course, and/or secure the vessel for severe wind and seas.

properties.title: Marine Weather Statement
properties.rawText:
Marine Weather Statement issued November 15 at 8:12PM PST by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA

A large west to northwesterly swell will produce a risk of
breaking waves at the Morro Bay and Ventura Harbor entrances
early Monday morning through late Monday night. These conditions
have a history of capsizing vessels of various sizes resulting in
serious injury or death, even to the most experienced mariners.

Mariners are urged to stay clear of these harbor entrances. For
more information, contact the local harbor patrol or coast guard
station and continue to monitor NOAA Weather Radio for the latest
weather information.

properties.title: Marine Weather Statement
properties.rawText:
Marine Weather Statement issued November 15 at 3:43PM HST by NWS Honolulu HI

A moderate, medium-period north swell from 350 to 360 degrees
moving through the islands will peak tonight and Monday as the
period shortens to 12 seconds. The swell will produce moderate to
heavy surges in north-facing harbors, especially at Kahului and
Hilo Harbors. Mariners using these harbors should exercise caution
when mooring or launching vessels and when entering or leaving
port. The swell will diminish Tuesday.

properties.title: Flood Warning
properties.rawText:
Flood Warning issued November 15 at 7:36PM CST until November 17 at 9:24PM CST by NWS Corpus Christi TX

...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Texas...

Nueces River Near Tilden affecting McMullen County.

For the Nueces River...including Cotulla, Tilden, Three Rivers,
Mathis, Bluntzer, Calallen...Moderate flooding is forecast.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...Nueces River near Tilden.

* WHEN...Until Tuesday evening.

* IMPACTS...At 16.0 feet, Moderate lowland flooding occurs. Hunting
cabins, oil field tanks and pumps are affected, and livestock
become isolated.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 6:30 PM CST Sunday the stage was 16.4 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 11.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is nearing its crest of 16.4 feet. It will
then fall below flood stage Tuesday morning.
- Flood stage is 14.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/crp.

properties.title: Flood Warning
properties.rawText:
Flood Warning issued November 16 at 9:44AM CST until November 17 at 11:48PM CST by NWS Corpus Christi TX

...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in Texas...

Nueces River Near Tilden affecting McMullen County.

For the Nueces River...including Cotulla, Tilden, Three Rivers,
Mathis, Bluntzer, Calallen...Moderate flooding is forecast.

- Forecast...The river is expected to fall below flood stage
tomorrow morning and continue falling to 4.1 feet Thursday
evening.
- Flood stage is 14.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/crp.

properties.title: Flood Warning
properties.rawText:
Flood Warning issued November 16 at 9:49AM EST by NWS Melbourne FL

...Forecast flooding changed from Minor to Moderate severity for the
following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Astor affecting Lake and Volusia Counties.

.Strong and persistent northerly winds are forecast later this week,
causing the St. Johns River at Astor to again rise into moderate
flood stage by the end of the work week.

For the St. Johns River...including Cocoa 9w, Above Lake Harney,
Astor...Major flooding is forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 3.0 feet, Water approaches or may enter lowest homes
on or near Wildhog Road and nearby canals. Flooding reaches the
parking lot of the Juno Trail Apartments. Flooding on portions of
Alligator Road and Holiday Road. Lowest lying yards along Blue
Creek are flooded. Roads at Astor Landing Campground and Lake
Dexter Boat Ramp begin to flood. Water enters lower homes closest
to the river on McPherson Lane.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:30 AM EST Monday the stage was 2.6 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 8:30 AM EST Monday was 2.6 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to remain steady above flood
stage at 2.6 feet.
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued this evening at 1100 PM EST.

additional heavy rainfall could delay this decline.

the Silver Pines subdivision in Rockledge and the Shakespeare Park

impassable, cutting off access to homes in the Mullet Lane and Bass
Road area. Docks flooded and water in parking lot at Lone Cabbage
Fish Camp.

produce moderate to heavy surges in north-facing harbors,
especially at Kahului and Hilo Harbors. Mariners using these
harbors should exercise caution when mooring or launching vessels
and when entering or leaving port. The swell will slowly diminish
later today through Tuesday.

properties.title: Hazardous Seas Warning
properties.rawText:
Hazardous Seas Warning issued November 16 at 2:27AM PST until November 16 at 4:00PM PST by NWS Medford OR

* WHAT...South to southwest winds 15 to 25 kt with very steep and
hazardous swell dominated seas 17 to 22 ft at 16 seconds. Swell
dominated seas lower late today into Tuesday, but remain steep
and hazardous 13 to 18 ft. Conditions worsen again Tuesday
afternoon. South winds increase with gales likely of 30 to 40 kt
with gusts up to 45 kt, and very steep and hazardous seas of 12
to 16 ft.

* WHERE...All areas.

* WHEN...For the Hazardous Seas Warning, until 4 PM PST this
afternoon. For the Small Craft Advisory, from 4 PM this
afternoon to 1 PM PST Tuesday. For the Gale Watch, from

properties.title: Yellow advisory · freezing drizzle advisory
properties.rawText:
Areas of freezing drizzle continue.

Freezing drizzle will continue today.

The freezing drizzle is expected to end later this afternoon or this evening .

Roads, walkways, and other surfaces will likely become icy and slippery.

Freezing drizzle advisories are issued when drizzle is expected to freeze on contact and create icy surfaces.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to NUstorm@ec.gc.ca, call 1-800-239-0484 or post reports on social media using #NUStorm.

properties.title: Yellow warning · blizzard warning
properties.rawText:
Prolonged blizzard conditions with near-zero visibility in blowing snow are expected.

What:
Near-zero visibility in blizzard conditions.

When:
Today.

Where:
Dempster Highway near the Richardson Mountains.

Additional information:
A persistent ridge of high pressure over the Beaufort Sea and a low pressure system over the Gulf of Alaska are generating strong winds across the Richardson Mountains. 

Easterly winds will strengthen this morning and reach gusts to 100 km/h this evening. Wind-swept snow and falling snow combined with the strong winds will result in blizzard conditions with near-zero visibility.

Road closures are possible.

If driving, turn on your lights, slow down and maintain a safe following distance.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to YTstorm@ec.gc.ca or post reports on social media using #YTStorm.

properties.title: Flood Warning
properties.rawText:
Flood Warning issued November 16 at 8:24PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL

...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Astor affecting Volusia and Lake Counties.

.On the St Johns River at Astor, slight rises within Minor Flood
Stage are forecast through at least midweek due to a combination of
northerly winds and water from upstream heavy rainfall working north
through the basin. Rises to Moderate Flood Stage are forecast later
in the week due to the heavy rainfall expected.

For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Minor to Moderate
flooding is forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor to moderate flooding
is forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.possible

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 3.0 feet, Water approaches or may enter lowest homes
on or near Wildhog Road and nearby canals. Flooding reaches the
parking lot of the Juno Trail Apartments. Flooding on portions of
Alligator Road and Holiday Road. Lowest lying yards along Blue
Creek are flooded. Roads at Astor Landing Campground and Lake
Dexter Boat Ramp begin to flood. Water enters lower homes closest
to the river on McPherson Lane.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:30 PM EST Monday the stage was 2.6 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 7:30 PM EST Monday was 2.6 feet.
- Forecast...The river is forecast to rise slightly through minor
flood stage into mid-week, possibly reaching moderate flood stage
by late week.
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking nethen northerly winds and upstream
tidal effects for forecast to slow or halt the decline. ar
riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued Tuesday morning at 1100 AM EST.

River levels are expected to remain nearly steady this week.

...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Cocoa 9w affecting Brevard County.

.Recent extreme rainfall over the headwaters of the St. Johns River
has caused the river near Cocoa to rise to Major Flood Stage. The
river is forecast to continue to remain steady with slight deviations
in river levels through mid to late week.

For the St. Johns River...including Cocoa 9w...Major flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Cocoa 9w.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 17.2 feet, Water enters homes along the St Johns River
in the Lake Poinsett area west of Cocoa, also low lying homes in
the Silver Pines subdivision in Rockledge and the Shakespeare Park
area of Cocoa. Providence Road area west of Cocoa becomes
impassable, cutting off access to homes in the Mullet Lane and Bass
Road area. Docks flooded and water in parking lot at Lone Cabbage
Fish Camp.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:15 PM EST Monday the stage was 17.1 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 15.8 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 7:15 PM EST Monday was 17.1 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to remain steady above flood
stage at 17.1 feet.
- Flood stage is 16.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued Tuesday morning at 1100 AM EST.

properties.title: special weather statement
properties.rawText:
Accumulating snow beginning Tuesday.

Snow at times heavy will develop Tuesday morning over southwestern Alberta and spread northward through the day, likely reaching Calgary in time for the evening commute. Snow will continue overnight and into Wednesday.

For areas further east, rain will change to snow overnight Tuesday. Total snowfall accumulations across all areas will be in the 5 to 15 cm range. The exact track and intensity of this system is still uncertain, so there is a possibility that some locations may be upgraded to a snowfall warning.

This snowfall event will end Wednesday night.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to ABstorm@ec.gc.ca, call 1-800-239-0484 or post reports on social media using #ABStorm.

properties.title: Yellow warning · snowfall warning
properties.rawText:
Heavy snowfall on Tuesday over southwestern Alberta.

Total snowfall amounts of 15 to 20 cm are expected. Initially rain or a rain snow mix will fall overnight tonight before changing to heavy snow Tuesday morning. The heaviest snow will fall Tuesday night into Wednesday afternoon.

This snow event will come to an end Wednesday night.

Roads and walkways will likely be difficult to navigate due to accumulating snow. There may be a significant impact on rush hour traffic.

If driving, turn on your lights, slow down and maintain a safe following distance.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to ABstorm@ec.gc.ca, call 1-800-239-0484 or post reports on social media using #ABStorm.

enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

properties.title: Yellow warning · blizzard warning
properties.rawText:
Prolonged blizzard conditions with near-zero visibility in snow and blowing snow continue.

What:
Near-zero visibility in blizzard conditions.

When:
Tonight

Where:
Dempster Highway near the Richardson Mountains.

Additional information:
A persistent ridge of high pressure over the Beaufort Sea and a low pressure system over the Gulf of Alaska are generating strong winds across the Richardson Mountains. 

Easterly winds with gusts to 100 km/h tonight. Wind-swept snow and falling snow combined with the strong winds will result in blizzard conditions with near-zero visibility.

properties.title: Special Marine Warning
properties.rawText:
Special Marine Warning issued November 17 at 1:06PM EST until November 17 at 2:00PM EST by NWS Key West FL

SMWKEY

The National Weather Service in Key West has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
Straits of Florida from Halfmoon Shoal to 20 nm west of Dry
Tortugas out 60 nm...
Gulf of Mexico including Dry Tortugas and Rebecca Shoal Channel...

* Until 200 PM EST.

* At 106 PM EST, a severe thunderstorm with possible waterspouts was
located 14 nm southwest of Tortugas Ecological Reserve South,
moving east at 10 knots.

HAZARD...Waterspouts, wind gusts 34 knots or greater, and large
hail.

SOURCE...Radar.

IMPACT...Waterspouts can quickly form and capsize boats, cause
considerable damage to vessels and create suddenly higher
waves. Expect wind gusts in excess of 34 knots, suddenly
higher waves, frequent lightning, and heavy downpours.
Large hail could result in injury and damage to boats.

* Locations in the warning include...
Tortugas Ecological Reserve South.

A waterspout is a tornado over water that can be dangerous and even
deadly. Small craft can be swamped or overturned by a waterspout,
avoid at all times.

Thunderstorms can produce sudden waterspouts. Waterspouts can easily
overturn boats and create locally hazardous seas. Seek safe harbor
immediately.

properties.title: Gale Warning
properties.rawText:
Gale Warning issued November 17 at 2:25AM PST until November 18 at 4:00AM PST by NWS Medford OR

* WHAT...Steep and hazardous swell dominated seas 13 to 18 ft at
16 seconds will lower to 10 to 14 ft this morning. Conditions
worsen again this afternoon. South winds increase to strong
gales 35 to 45 kt with gusts up to 50 kt. A brief period of
storm force gusts are possible this evening. Seas will build,
becoming very steep and hazardous at 14 to 17 ft at 13 seconds
through early Wednesday.

* WHERE...All areas.

* WHEN...For the Small Craft Advisory, until 1 PM PST this
afternoon. For the Gale Warning, from 1 PM this afternoon to 4
AM PST Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...Strong winds and very steep seas could capsize or
damage vessels. Low visibility conditions are expected.

Mariners should alter plans to avoid strong winds and very steep
seas. Remain in port, seek safe harbor, alter course, and/or
secure the vessel for severe conditions.

properties.title: special weather statement
properties.rawText:
Accumulating snow will begin this afternoon or evening. 

Total snowfall accumulations are expected to be in the 5 to 10 cm range. 

Snowfall will taper off Wednesday evening.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to ABstorm@ec.gc.ca, call 1-800-239-0484 or post reports on social media using #ABStorm.
