properties.title: Yellow warning · snowfall warning
properties.rawText:
An extended period of snowfall, at times heavy, is expected. 20 to 40 cm of snowfall accumulation is expected.

A low-pressure system moving into Baffin Bay is bringing snow to Qikiqtarjuaq, lasting until Thursday morning. The snow will be light today but will slowly ramp up before becoming heavy on Wednesday. Strong northwest winds gusting up to 70 km/h will begin to pick up tonight, reducing visibilities in blowing snow.

The snow and winds will taper off Thursday morning.

Visibility will likely be reduced at times.

Prepare for quickly changing and deteriorating travel conditions.

Snowfall warnings are issued when significant impacts are expected due to snowfall accumulations.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to NUstorm@ec.gc.ca, call 1-800-239-0484 or post reports on social media using #NUStorm.

properties.title: Yellow warning · snowfall warning
properties.rawText:
Snow at times heavy continues over southwestern Alberta. 

This snow will spread north and east through the day. Areas near the Saskatchewan border will begin as rain before changing to heavy snow this evening.

General snowfall totals of 15 to 20 cm are expected, with Calgary on the lower end of this range. More favoured locations such as the foothills, the  Cypress Hills, rural areas of southern Alberta near Brooks-Medicine Hat-Lethbridge may see snowfall amounts near 25 cm. 

Snowfall will taper off Wednesday evening.

Travel will likely be challenging. Roads and walkways will likely be difficult to navigate due to accumulating snow. There may be a significant impact on rush hour traffic.

Prepare for quickly changing and deteriorating travel conditions. If driving, turn on your lights, slow down and maintain a safe following distance.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to ABstorm@ec.gc.ca, call 1-800-239-0484 or post reports on social media using #ABStorm.

properties.title: Yellow warning · wind warning
properties.rawText:
High northwesterly winds with gusts up to 90 kilometers per hour are expected. These winds will ease this evening.

Local utility outages are possible. Disruptions to services and travel are possible.

Secure loose objects.

Wind warnings are issued when there is a significant risk of damaging winds.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to QCstorm@ec.gc.ca or post reports on social media using #QCStorm.

properties.title: Yellow warning · wind warning
properties.rawText:
Damaging winds are expected.

Locations: Northern Peninsula East.

Maximum wind gusts: southwesterly 70 km/h, except 100 in the Canada Bay area.

Time span: early this evening until after midnight tonight.

Damage to roofs, fences, branches or soft shelters is possible.

Secure loose objects.

Wind warnings are issued when there is a significant risk of damaging winds.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to NLstorm@ec.gc.ca or post reports on social media using #NLwx.

Operating Restrictions and Requirements
No pilots may operate an aircraft in the areas covered by this NOTAM (except as described).
EXC AS SPECIFIED BLW AND/OR UNLESS AUTH BY ATC IN CONSULTATION WITH THE AIR TFC SECURITY COORDINATOR VIA THE DOMESTIC EVENTS NETWORK (DEN):
A. ALL ACFT OPS WI THE 10NM RADIUS AREA(S) LISTED ABV, KNOWN AS THE INNER CORE(S), ARE PROHIBITED EXC FOR: APPROVED LAW ENFORCEMENT, MIL ACFT DIRECTLY SUPPORTING THE UNITED STATES SECRET SERVICE(USSS) AND THE OFFICE OF THE PRESIDENT OF THE UNITED STATES, APPROVED AIR AMBULANCE FLIGHTS, AND REGULARLY SCHEDULED COMMERCIAL PAX AND ALL - CARGO CARRIERS OPR UNDER ONE OF THE FOLLOWING TSA - APPROVED STANDARD SECURITY PROGRAMS / PROC AND ARE ARR INTO AND / OR DEP FM 14 CFR PART 139 AP: ACFT OPR STANDARD SECURITY PROGRAM(AOSSP), FULL ALL - CARGO ACFT OPR STANDARD SECURITY PROGRAM(FACAOSSP), MODEL SECURITY PROGRAM(MSP), TWELVE FIVE STANDARD SECURITY PROGRAM ALL CARGO(TFSSP - ALL CARGO), OR ALL - CARGO INTERNATIONAL SECURITY PROC(ACISP). ALL EMERGENCY / LIFE SAVING FLT(MEDICAL / LAW ENFORCEMENT / FIREFIGHTING) OPS MUST COORDINATE WITH ATC PRIOR TO THEIR DEP AT 907-271-2711 TO AVOID POTENTIAL DELAYS.
B. FOR OPS WI THE AIRSPACE BTN THE 10NM RADIUS AND 30NM RADIUS AREA(S) LISTED ABV, KNOWN AS THE OUTER RING(S): ALL ACFT OPR WI THE OUTER RING(S) LISTED ABV ARE LIMITED TO ACFT ARR OR DEP LOCAL AIRFIELDS, AND WORKLOAD PERMITTING, ATC MAY AUTHORIZE TRANSIT OPS. ACFT MAY NOT LOITER. ALL ACFT MUST BE ON AN ACT IFR OR FILED VFR FLT PLAN WITH A DISCRETE CODE ASSIGNED BY AN AIR TFC CTL (ATC) FAC. ACFT MUST BE SQUAWKING THE DISCRETE CODE PRIOR TO DEP AND AT ALL TIMES WHILE IN THE TFR AND MUST REMAIN IN TWO-WAY RADIO COM WITH ATC.
C. THE FOLLOWING OPS ARE NOT AUTH WI THIS TFR: FLT TRAINING, PRACTICE INSTRUMENT APCH, AEROBATIC FLT, GLIDER OPS, PARACHUTE OPS, ULTRALIGHT, HANG GLIDING, BALLOON OPS, AGRICULTURE/CROP DUSTING, ANIMAL POPULATION CTL FLT OPS, BANNER TOWING OPS, SIGHTSEEING OPS, MAINTENANCE TEST FLIGHTS, MODEL ACFT OPS, MODEL ROCKETRY, UNMANNED ACFT SYSTEMS (UAS), AND UTILITY AND PIPELINE SURVEY OPS.
D. UAS OPR WHO DO NOT COMPLY WITH APPLICABLE AIRSPACE RESTRICTIONS ARE WARNED THAT PURSUANT TO 10 U.S.C.SECTION 130I AND 6 U.S.C.SECTION 124N, THE DEPARTMENT OF DEFENSE(DOD), THE DEPARTMENT OF HOMELAND SECURITY(DHS) OR THE DEPARTMENT OF JUSTICE(DOJ) MAY TAKE SECURITY ACTION THAT RESULTS IN THE INTERFERENCE, DISRUPTION, SEIZURE, DAMAGING, OR DESTRUCTION OF UNMANNED ACFT DEEMED TO POSE A CREDIBLE SAFETY OR SECURITY THREAT TO PROTECTED PERSONNEL, FAC, OR ASSETS.
E. THE SYSTEM OPERATIONS SUPPORT CENTER (SOSC), IS THE CDN FAC FOR UAS OPS, SUBMIT SGI WAIVER REQUEST VIA HTTPS://WAIVERS.FAA.GOV, FIRST RESPONDERS EMGERGENCY OPS CTC THE SOSC AT 202-267-8276.
F. THE FAA RECOMMENDS THAT ALL ACFT OPR CK NOTAMS FREQUENTLY FOR POSSIBLE CHANGES TO THIS TFR PRIOR TO OPS. OPR MAY REVIEW THE TFR DETAILS AT HTTPS://TFR.FAA.GOV/ OR HTTPS://WWW.1800WXBRIEF.COM.

properties.title: Flood Warning
properties.rawText:
Flood Warning issued November 17 at 8:17PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL

...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Cocoa 9w affecting Brevard County.

.Recent extreme rainfall over the headwaters of the St. Johns River
has caused the river near Cocoa to rise to Major Flood Stage. The
river is forecast to continue to remain steady with slight deviations
in river levels through mid to late week due to additional forecast
heavy rainfall.

For the St. Johns River...including Cocoa 9w...Major flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Cocoa 9w.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 17.2 feet, Water enters homes along the St Johns River
in the Lake Poinsett area west of Cocoa, also low lying homes in
the Silver Pines subdivision in Rockledge and the Shakespeare Park
area of Cocoa. Providence Road area west of Cocoa becomes
impassable, cutting off access to homes in the Mullet Lane and Bass
Road area. Docks flooded and water in parking lot at Lone Cabbage
Fish Camp.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:15 PM EST Tuesday the stage was 17.1 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 15.8 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 7:15 PM EST Tuesday was 17.1 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to remain steady above flood
stage at 17.1 feet.
- Flood stage is 16.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued Wednesday morning at 1100 AM EST.

properties.title: Special Marine Warning
properties.rawText:
Special Marine Warning issued November 17 at 8:01PM EST until November 17 at 9:00PM EST by NWS Miami FL

SMWMFL

The National Weather Service in Miami has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
Biscayne Bay...
Coastal waters from Deerfield Beach to Ocean Reef FL out 20 NM...
Coastal waters from Jupiter Inlet to Deerfield Beach FL out 20
NM...

* Until 900 PM EST.

* At 801 PM EST, a severe thunderstorm capable of producing
waterspouts was located 7 nm east of Port Everglades, or 7 nm
southeast of Lauderdale-By-The-Sea, moving west at 15 knots.

HAZARD...Waterspouts and wind gusts 34 knots or greater.

SOURCE...Radar.

IMPACT...Waterspouts can easily overturn boats and create locally
hazardous seas. Small craft could be damaged in briefly
higher winds and suddenly higher waves.

* Locations impacted include...
Sunny Isles, Lauderdale-By-The-Sea, Hallandale, Fort Lauderdale,
Lighthouse Point, Hillsboro Beach, Bay Harbor Islands, Port
Everglades, Sea Ranch Lakes, Bal Harbour, Golden Beach, Surfside,
Indian Creek, Pompano Beach, Hollywood, Deerfield Beach, Boca
Raton, and Miami Beach.

Move to safe harbor until hazardous weather passes.

Thunderstorms can produce sudden waterspouts. Waterspouts can easily
overturn boats and create locally hazardous seas. Seek safe harbor
immediately.

Report severe weather to the Coast Guard or the National Weather
Service. You can also share your report with NWS Miami on Facebook
and Twitter.
properties.stationOrArea: Biscayne Bay; Coastal waters from Jupiter Inlet to Deerfield Beach FL out 20 NM; Coastal waters from Deerfield Beach to Ocean Reef FL out 20 NM

properties.title: Special Marine Warning
properties.rawText:
Special Marine Warning issued November 17 at 7:58PM EST until November 17 at 9:00PM EST by NWS Key West FL

SMWKEY

The National Weather Service in Key West has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
Hawk Channel and Straits of Florida from west end of Seven Mile
Bridge to Halfmoon Shoal out 20 nm...
Gulf Waters from East Cape Sable to Chokoloskee 20 to 60 nm out and
beyond 5 fathoms...
Gulf of America from west end of Seven Mile Bridge to Halfmoon
Shoal out to 5 fathoms...

* Until 900 PM EST.

* At 758 PM EST, severe thunderstorms with possible waterspouts were
located along a line extending from 8 nm north of Ellis Rock Light
to 6 nm east of Halfmoon Shoal Light, moving south at 5 knots.

HAZARD...Waterspouts, wind gusts 34 knots or greater, and large
hail.

SOURCE...National Weather Service Meteorologist.

IMPACT...Waterspouts can quickly form and capsize boats, cause
considerable damage to vessels and create suddenly higher
waves. Expect wind gusts in excess of 34 knots, suddenly
higher waves, frequent lightning, and heavy downpours.
Large hail could result in injury and damage to boats.

* Locations in the warning include...
Ellis Rock Light, New Ground Rocks Light, and Marquesas Keys.

Boaters should seek safe harbor as quickly, and as safely as
possible. When downpours reduce visibility, slow down.

properties.title: Flash Flood Warning
properties.rawText:
Flash Flood Warning issued November 17 at 7:53PM EST until November 17 at 10:00PM EST by NWS Miami FL

FFWMFL

The National Weather Service in Miami has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Northern Broward County in southeastern Florida...

* Until 1000 PM EST.

* At 753 PM EST, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across the warned area. Between 2 and 4 inches of rain
have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts of 1 to 3 inches are
possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected
to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Coral Springs, Tamarac, Margate, Lauderhill, Coconut Creek, North
Lauderdale, Lauderdale Lakes, Parkland, Broadview-Pompano Park,
Godfrey Road, Village Park, Palm Aire and Ramblewood East.

Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

properties.title: Marine Weather Statement
properties.rawText:
Marine Weather Statement issued November 17 at 7:44PM EST by NWS Key West FL

At 840 pm, a number of clusters of strong showers and thunderstorms
were located across the near and offshore waters west of the Lower
Keys. Movement of this activity has been chaotic at 10 to 15 knots.
This activity will generally produce wind gusts near 30 knots, at

properties.title: Flood Warning
properties.rawText:
Flood Warning issued November 17 at 5:40PM MST until November 17 at 11:15PM MST by NWS Flagstaff AZ

* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Munds Canyon and Oak Creek near Sedona.

* WHEN...Until 1115 PM MST.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of creeks and normally dry washes is occurring.
Deadly flooding over low-water crossings.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 532 PM MST, river gauges at Munds Canyon and Oak Creek near
Sedona have both crested. However, water levels will remain
elevated over the next few hours as water gradually decreases.
- This includes the following creeks, washes and rivers...
Oak Creek and Dry Beaver Creek.
- For Oak Creek at Sedona:
At 4:45pm the stage was 8.23 feet.
Flood Stage is 14.0 feet.
Forecast: A crest of 8.43 feet is expected by 7:00pm Tuesday.
Impacts:
At 5.0 feet: Multiple private low water crossings and bridges
over Oak Creek above Sedona become impassable.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Sedona, Munds Park, Indian Gardens, Uptown Sedona, Red Rock State
Park and Cathedral Rock.
- This includes the following swimming holes...
Midgely Bridge, Buddha Beach "Red Rock Crossing" and Crescent
Moon Ranch.
- Additional information is available at weather.gov/flagstaff.

Stay away or be swept away! The banks of creeks and washes are
unstable and unsafe during any flooding event.

Low water crossings will be dangerous. Do not attempt to cross
flooded roads. Find an alternate route.

Special Marine Warning issued November 17 at 7:33PM EST until November 17 at 8:30PM EST by NWS Key West FL

The National Weather Service in Key West has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
Gulf Waters from East Cape Sable to Chokoloskee 20 to 60 nm out and
beyond 5 fathoms...
Gulf of America from west end of Seven Mile Bridge to Halfmoon
Shoal out to 5 fathoms...
Gulf of America including Dry Tortugas and Rebecca Shoal Channel...

* Until 830 PM EST.

* At 733 PM EST, a strong thunderstorm was located over New Ground
Rocks Light, moving northwest at 5 knots.

HAZARD...Wind gusts 34 knots or greater.

SOURCE...National Weather Service Meteorologist.

IMPACT...Expect wind gusts in excess of 34 knots, suddenly higher
waves, frequent lightning, and heavy downpours.

* Locations in the warning include...
New Ground Rocks Light.

Boaters should seek safe harbor as quickly, and as safely as
possible. When downpours reduce visibility, slow down.

properties.title: Flash Flood Warning
properties.rawText:
Flash Flood Warning issued November 17 at 5:20PM MST until November 17 at 9:15PM MST by NWS Flagstaff AZ

At 520 PM MST, a rise of 6 feet has occurred upstream of Page Springs
at Sedona. The guage at Cornville has begun to rise, with a further
rise expected in the next few hours. Flash flooding is already
occurring.

Flash flooding is expected to begin along Oak Creek in the Page
Springs area within the next few hours.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding.

SOURCE...River gauge reported.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of Oak Creek.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Cornville, Jordan, Page Springs and Bignotti.

For Oak Creek at Cornville:
At 5:00pm the stage was 2.01 feet.
Flood Stage is 8.0 feet.
Forecast: A crest of 9.17 feet is expected at 9:00pm Tuesday.
Impacts:
At 7.0 feet: Flooding begins to inundate lower terrace of RV park
upstream of Page Springs Road Bridge.
At 8.0 feet: Flooding of lower terrace of RV park upstream of Page
Springs Road Bridge.
At 9.0 feet: Hiking trails along banks of creek affected. Portions of
residential yards flooded.

This includes the following recreation areas and campgrounds...
Windmill Park.

This includes the following swimming holes...
Mormons Crossing.

This includes the following creeks, washes and rivers...
Oak Creek.

Move to higher ground now. Act quickly to protect your life.

Stay away or be swept away! The banks of creeks and washes are
unstable and unsafe during any flooding event.

Low water crossings will become dangerous in heavy rain. Do not
attempt to cross flooded roads. Find an alternate route.

properties.title: special weather statement
properties.rawText:
Accumulating snow beginning Wednesday.

The first significant snowfall of the season is expected for southwest Saskatchewan.

A low-pressure system will bring an area of precipitation to southwestern Saskatchewan beginning this evening. The precipitation will likely begin as rain, but will slowly change over to snow or a rain/snow mix tonight as it spreads eastward. Total snowfall accumulations are expected to be in the 5 to 15 cm range for most areas. The snow will be heavy at times on Wednesday before slowly tapering off through Wednesday night.

The snowfall will end by Thursday morning.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to SKstorm@ec.gc.ca, call 1-800-239-0484 or post reports on social media using #SKStorm.

properties.title: Yellow warning · air quality warning
properties.rawText:
Elevated pollution levels are expected or occurring.

17th November 2026 - The Ministry of Environment and Parks in collaboration with the Northern Health Authority has issued an Air Quality Warning for Vanderhoof due to elevated coarse particulate matter.

Exposure to coarse particulate matter is particularly a concern for infants, older adults, individuals with chronic conditions (such as asthma, COPD, heart disease, and diabetes) or respiratory infections, and those who are pregnant.

Postpone or reduce strenuous outdoors activities until the warning has ended. Spend time indoors in a space with filtered air. Monitor your symptoms and seek prompt medical attention if needed.

Current conditions are expected to persist until weather conditions change and/or local emissions are reduced.

The next update will be on November 18, 2026 and posted to the province's Air Quality Warnings webpage.

Visit the provincial air quality data webpage for real-time observations.

Visit https://www.airhealth.ca for information on how to reduce your health risk and your personal contribution to pollution levels, as well as for current and forecast AQHI values.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada.

Issued by Environment Canada and the B.C. Ministry of Environment and Parks

properties.title: Yellow warning · snowfall warning
properties.rawText:
Snow at times heavy continues over southern Alberta. 

This snow will spread north and east. Areas near the Saskatchewan border will begin as rain before changing to heavy snow tonight.

General snowfall totals of 15 to 20 cm are expected, with Calgary on the lower end of this range. More favoured locations such as the foothills, the  Cypress Hills, rural areas of southern Alberta near Brooks-Medicine Hat-Lethbridge may see snowfall amounts near 25 cm. 

Snowfall will taper off Wednesday evening.

Travel will likely be challenging. Roads and walkways will likely be difficult to navigate due to accumulating snow. There may be a significant impact on rush hour traffic.

Prepare for quickly changing and deteriorating travel conditions. If driving, turn on your lights, slow down and maintain a safe following distance.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to ABstorm@ec.gc.ca, call 1-800-239-0484 or post reports on social media using #ABStorm.

Blizzard conditions will develop tonight in Clyde River when snow and strengthening winds out of the northwest develop.

Maximum wind gusts: Northwesterly 60 to 80 km/h.

Travel will likely be hazardous in some locations. Travel will likely be hazardous.

properties.title: Orange warning · snowfall warning
properties.rawText:
An extended period of snowfall, at times heavy, will continue. 30 to 50 cm of snowfall accumulation is expected.

A low-pressure system moving into Baffin Bay is bringing snow to Qikiqtarjuaq, lasting until Thursday morning. The snow will intensify tonight before becoming heavy on Wednesday. Strong northwest winds gusting up to 70 km/h will begin to pick up tonight, reducing visibilities in blowing snow.

The snow and winds will taper off Thursday morning.

Travel will likely be hazardous. Visibility will likely be reduced at times.

Snowfall warnings are issued when significant impacts are expected due to snowfall accumulations.

properties.title: Special Marine Warning
properties.rawText:
Special Marine Warning issued November 18 at 3:26AM EST until November 18 at 4:30AM EST by NWS Key West FL

SMWKEY

The National Weather Service in Key West has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
Straits of Florida from west end of Seven Mile Bridge to Halfmoon
Shoal out 60 nm...

* Until 430 AM EST.

* At 326 AM EST, a strong thunderstorm with possible waterspouts was
located 18 nm south of Twenty-Eight Foot Shoal Light. The strong
thunderstorm was nearly stationary.

HAZARD...Waterspouts and wind gusts 34 knots or greater.

SOURCE...National Weather Service Meteorologist.

IMPACT...Waterspouts can quickly form and capsize boats, cause
considerable damage to vessels and create suddenly higher
waves. Expect wind gusts in excess of 34 knots, suddenly
higher waves, frequent lightning, and heavy downpours.

* The strong thunderstorm will remain over mainly open waters.

Prepare for wind gusts in excess of 34 knots, steep and fast-building
seas, frequent lightning, and blinding downpours. Stay low or go
below, and make sure all on board are wearing life jackets.

Thunderstorms can produce sudden waterspouts. Waterspouts can easily
overturn boats and create locally hazardous seas. Seek safe harbor
immediately.
properties.stationOrArea: Straits of Florida from west end of Seven Mile Bridge to south of Halfmoon Shoal out 20 NM; Straits of Florida from west end of Seven Mile Bridge to south of Halfmoon Shoal 20 to 60 NM out

properties.title: Hazardous Seas Warning
properties.rawText:
Hazardous Seas Warning issued November 18 at 12:17AM PST until November 18 at 10:00PM PST by NWS Portland OR

* WHAT...For the Gale Warning, seas 10 to 14 ft at 10 seconds and
southeast winds 20 to 30 kt with gusts up to 40 kt. For the
Hazardous Seas Warning, very steep and hazardous seas 12 to 15
ft at 14 seconds and southeast winds 15 to 25 kt with gusts up
to 30 kt expected.

* WHERE...Outer Coastal Waters from Cape Shoalwater to Florence
10 to 60 NM offshore.

* WHEN...Gale Warning, until 4 AM PST early this morning.
Hazardous Seas Warning, from 4 AM early this morning to 10 PM
PST this evening.

* IMPACTS...Strong winds will cause hazardous seas which could
capsize or damage vessels and reduce visibility.

A Gale Warning means winds of 34 to 47 knots are imminent or
occurring. Operating a vessel in gale conditions requires
experience and properly equipped vessels. It is highly
recommended that mariners without the proper experience seek safe
harbor prior to the onset of gale conditions.

properties.title: Marine Weather Statement
properties.rawText:
Marine Weather Statement issued November 18 at 2:29AM EST by NWS Key West FL

At 230 am, a large swath of strong winds with frequent easterly wind
gusts near 40 knots blanketed the near and offshore waters gulf side
of the Lower Keys, as well as the adjacent nearshore waters to the
south. These winds will spread east southeastward across the Lower
Keys and into the Middle Keys and surrounding nearshore waters over
the next hour, then gradually diminish.

Elsewhere, numerous clusters of showers and a few embedded
thunderstorms were located over the near and offshore waters west of
the Lower Keys. This activity has generally been moving
northeastward at 10 to 15 knots. The stronger activity will produce
wind gusts near 30 knots, occasional lightning strikes, and blinding
downpours. Some of these cells may rapidly intensify and strong
waterspouts will be possible, requiring a Special Marine Warning.

thunderstorms were located over the near and offshore waters west of
the Lower Keys. This activity has been moving northward at 15 to 20
knots. The stronger activity will produce wind gusts near 30 knots,
occasional lightning strikes, and blinding downpours. Some of these
cells may rapidly intensify, requiring a Special Marine Warning.

properties.title: Flood Warning
properties.rawText:
Flood Warning issued November 17 at 8:20PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL

...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Astor affecting Volusia and Lake Counties.

.On the St Johns River at Astor, slight rises within Minor Flood
Stage are forecast through at least midweek due to a combination of
northerly winds and water from upstream heavy rainfall working north
through the basin. Rises to Moderate Flood Stage are forecast later
in the week due to the additional heavy rainfall expected.

For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Minor flooding is
occurring and moderate flooding is forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 3.5 feet, Canals have overflowed into yards. Homes on
or near Wildhog, Bonnet and Snail roads become inaccessible with
several inches of water inside homes along the river and canals.
Docks at Astor Bridge marina and throughout Astor are completely
submerged. Bartram Rd and Holiday Circle are inaccessible with
yards completely submerged. Clair Street is inaccessible. Roads
flooded in South Moon Fish Camp, docks and yards at condominiums on
Juno Trail and water breaches the sea wall at Blair's Jungle Den.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:30 PM EST Tuesday the stage was 2.7 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 7:30 PM EST Tuesday was 2.7 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to 3.4 feet Sunday
morning. Additional rises are possible thereafter.
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued Wednesday morning at 1100 AM EST.

properties.title: special weather statement

Accumulating snow will continue tonight and Wednesday, with total amounts of 5 to 10 cm.

Snowfall will taper off Wednesday evening.

Prepare for quickly changing and deteriorating travel conditions.

properties.title: Orange warning · blizzard warning
properties.rawText:
Blizzard conditions with near-zero visibility in blowing snow are expected.

Blizzard conditions are expected to develop in Qikiqtarjuaq Wednesday morning, as very heavy snow combines with winds gusting to 80 km/h to give zero to near-zero visibility in snow and blowing snow.  The blizzard will continue through the day Wednesday before tapering off overnight into Thursday morning. Total snowfall accumulation of 25 to 50 cm are expected.

If you become lost or stranded, remain where you are until conditions improve.

properties.title: Marine Weather Statement
properties.rawText:
Marine Weather Statement issued November 18 at 11:29AM EST by NWS Key West FL

At 1130 am, widespread showers are ongoing across the Florida Keys
and surrounding near and offshore waters within a mesoscale
convective complex. This activity is producing pockets of higher
wind gusts of 25 to near 34 knots and reduced visibility from
moderate to heavy downpours. Lightning frequency is decreasing
substantially. Activity is slowly propagating eastward and
circulating around a small scale area of low pressure currently
centered in the Straits of Florida approximately 32 nautical miles
southeast of Key West. Showers are diminishing from west to east, and
rain has ended in the waters near Key West, but strong to briefly
gale force easterly wind gusts are occurring along the western
periphery of the decaying precipitation near the Lower Keys.

properties.rawText:
Hazardous Seas Warning issued November 18 at 4:07AM PST until November 18 at 10:00PM PST by NWS Portland OR

* WHAT...For the Hazardous Seas Warning, very steep and hazardous
seas 12 to 15 ft at 14 seconds and southeast winds 15 to 25 kt
with gusts up to 30 kt. For the Small Craft Advisory, seas 9 to
14 ft at 14 seconds and east winds 5 to 10 kt expected.

* WHERE...Outer Coastal Waters from Cape Shoalwater to Florence
10 to 60 NM offshore.

* WHEN...Hazardous Seas Warning, until 10 PM PST this evening.
Small Craft Advisory, from 10 PM this evening to 10 AM PST
Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Very steep and hazardous seas could capsize or cause
damage to vessels.

A Hazardous Seas Warning means hazardous sea conditions are
imminent or occurring. Recreational boaters should remain in
port, or take shelter until waves subside.  Commercial vessels
should prepare for rough seas and consider remaining in port or
taking shelter in port until hazardous seas subside.

properties.title: Yellow warning · air quality warning
properties.rawText:
Elevated pollution levels are expected or occurring.

17th November 2026 - The Ministry of Environment and Parks in collaboration with the Northern Health Authority has issued an Air Quality Warning for Vanderhoof due to elevated coarse particulate matter.

Exposure to coarse particulate matter is particularly a concern for infants, older adults, individuals with chronic conditions (such as asthma, COPD, heart disease, and diabetes) or respiratory infections, and those who are pregnant.

Postpone or reduce strenuous outdoors activities until the warning has ended. Spend time indoors in a space with filtered air. Monitor your symptoms and seek prompt medical attention if needed.

Current conditions are expected to persist until weather conditions change and/or local emissions are reduced.

The next update will be on November 18, 2026 and posted to the province's Air Quality Warnings webpage.

Visit the provincial air quality data webpage for real-time observations.

Visit https://www.airhealth.ca for information on how to reduce your health risk and your personal contribution to pollution levels, as well as for current and forecast AQHI values.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada.

Issued by Environment Canada and the B.C. Ministry of Environment and Parks

Blizzard conditions which developed last evening will improve this morning as winds diminish and the snow tapers off.  However, strengthening winds late this afternoon will bring a return to blizzard conditions, with near-zero visibility in blowing snow and gusts to 90  km/h expected to persist throughout the night.  The blizzard will taper off Thursday morning.

Limit travel and outdoor activities, if possible.

properties.title: Orange warning · blizzard warning
properties.rawText:
Blizzard conditions with near-zero visibility in snow and blowing snow continue.

Blizzard conditions have developed in Qikiqtarjuaq this morning, as very heavy snow combines with winds gusting up to 90 km/h to give zero to near-zero visibility in snow and blowing snow.  The blizzard will continue through the day before tapering off overnight into Thursday morning. Total snowfall accumulation of 30 to 50 cm are expected.

Travel will be dangerous and likely impossible due to near-zero visibility.

If you become lost or stranded, remain where you are until conditions improve.

properties.title: Marine Weather Statement
properties.rawText:
Marine Weather Statement issued November 18 at 6:33PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL

A Marine Weather Statement has been issued for the following areas...
Volusia-Brevard County Line to Sebastian Inlet 0-20 nm...
Volusia-Brevard County Line to Sebastian Inlet 20-60 nm...

* At 633 PM EST, Doppler radar indicated a shower, capable of
producing winds to around 30 knots. A waterspout is possible, and
trends are being monitored for a Special Marine Warning. This a
shower was located 16 NM east of Port Canaveral, moving west at 20
knots.

Locations impacted include...
Port Canaveral, Jetty Park, Cape Canaveral, Cocoa Beach, Patrick
Space Force Base, Merritt Island, Georgiana, Playalinda Beach,
Pineda, Rockledge and Cocoa.

Mariners can expect gusty winds to around 30 knots, locally higher
waves, lightning strikes, and heavy downpours. Boaters should seek
safe harbor immediately until this storm passes.

Special Marine Warning issued November 18 at 6:02PM EST until November 18 at 7:00PM EST by NWS Miami FL

SMWMFL

The National Weather Service in Miami has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
Coastal waters from Deerfield Beach to Ocean Reef FL out 20 NM...
Waters from Deerfield Beach to Ocean Reef FL from 20 to 60 NM
excluding the territorial waters of Bahamas...

* Until 700 PM EST.

* At 602 PM EST, a severe thunderstorm capable of producing
waterspouts was located 26 nm southeast of Carysfort Reef Light,
moving northwest at 15 knots.

SOURCE...Radar.

hazardous seas. Small craft could be damaged in briefly
higher winds and suddenly higher waves.

overturn boats and create locally hazardous seas. Seek safe harbor
immediately.

Report severe weather to the Coast Guard or the National Weather
Service. You can also share your report with NWS Miami on Facebook
and Twitter.

properties.title: Flood Warning
properties.rawText:
Flood Warning issued November 18 at 2:41PM PST until November 18 at 4:45PM PST by NWS San Francisco CA

* WHAT...Urban areas and small streams flooding caused by excessive
rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Alameda and Contra Costa Counties...

* WHEN...Until 445 PM PST.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is imminent or occurring.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 240 PM PST, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges indicated
heavy rain. Flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly in
the warned area. Between 1 and 2 inches of rain have fallen.
- Additional rainfall amounts of 0.5 to 1 inch are possible in the
warned area.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Oakland, Fremont, Hayward, Concord, Richmond, Antioch, Livermore,
San Ramon, Pleasanton, Union City, Walnut Creek, Pittsburg,
Dublin, Danville, Martinez, Oakley, Pleasant Hill and San Pablo.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

Stay away or be swept away. River banks and culverts can become
unstable and unsafe.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

properties.title: Flash Flood Warning
properties.rawText:
Flash Flood Warning issued November 18 at 2:30PM PST until November 18 at 5:30PM PST by NWS San Francisco CA

FFWMTR

The National Weather Service in San Francisco has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
The Timber burn area...

* Until 530 PM PST.

* At 230 PM PST, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges indicated
heavy rain falling over the Timber Burn Area. Between 1 and 2
inches of rain have fallen. The expected rainfall rate is 0.5 to
0.75 inches in 1 hour. Additional rainfall amounts of 1 to 3 inches
are possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or
expected to begin shortly. Excessive rainfall over the burn scar
will result in debris flow moving through the Drainages within
Lafler, Castro and Graves Canyons, as well as drainages between
Grimes and Castro Canyons. The debris flow can consist of rock,
mud, vegetation and other loose materials.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Heavy rain producing
flash flooding in and around the Timber Burn Area.

SOURCE...Radar and automated gauges.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of areas in and around the
Timber Burn Area.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
portions of CA Highway 1 and the Los Padres National Forecast from
Andrew Molera State Park to Partington Ridge including the town of
Big Sur.

Move away from recently burned areas. Life-threatening flooding of
creeks, and roads is likely. The heavy rains will likely trigger
rockslides, mudslides, and debris flows in steep terrain. Impacted
areas include locations along Highway 1 near mile marker 50 south of
Andrew Molera State Park to mile maker 38. Other areas impacted
include Pfeiffer Big Sur State Park Campground and Partington Ridge,
structures along the Big Sur River, Mule Creek Canyon, and adjacent
drainages and watershed outlets.

properties.rawText:

...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Sanford affecting Seminole County.

.Additional heavy rainfall over the next few days has brought the St
Johns River at Sanford into Minor flood stage today with a slow climb
continuing into next week.

forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Sanford.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 6.2 feet, Water completely surrounds many homes in the
Stone Island and Still Brook subdivisions. Pool enclosures and
patios become flooded. Water covers many of the roads. Flooding
occurs on Enterprise Road and in the Bethel Loop subdivision.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 2:30 PM EST Wednesday the stage was 5.6 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 4.2 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 2:30 PM EST Wednesday was 5.6 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to 6.2 feet Monday
morning. Additional rises are possible thereafter.
- Flood stage is 5.5 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

through flooded areas.

properties.title: Yellow warning · air quality warning
properties.rawText:
Elevated pollution levels are expected or occurring.

17th November 2026 - The Ministry of Environment and Parks in collaboration with the Northern Health Authority has issued an Air Quality Warning for Vanderhoof due to elevated coarse particulate matter.

Exposure to coarse particulate matter is particularly a concern for infants, older adults, individuals with chronic conditions (such as asthma, COPD, heart disease, and diabetes) or respiratory infections, and those who are pregnant.

Postpone or reduce strenuous outdoors activities until the warning has ended. Spend time indoors in a space with filtered air. Monitor your symptoms and seek prompt medical attention if needed.

Current conditions are expected to persist until weather conditions change and/or local emissions are reduced.

The next update will be on November 19, 2026 and posted to the province's Air Quality Warnings webpage.

Visit the provincial air quality data webpage for real-time observations.

Visit https://www.airhealth.ca for information on how to reduce your health risk and your personal contribution to pollution levels, as well as for current and forecast AQHI values.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada.

Issued by Environment Canada and the B.C. Ministry of Environment and Parks

Snow at times heavy continues over southeastern Alberta.

Snow will continue late this afternoon into the evening, with an additional 2 to 4 cm expected and total accumulations reaching locally 10 to 20 cm.

properties.title: Flash Flood Warning
properties.rawText:
Flash Flood Warning issued November 18 at 7:47PM PST until November 18 at 10:00PM PST by NWS San Francisco CA

FFWMTR

The National Weather Service in San Francisco has extended the

* Flash Flood Warning for...
The Plaskett burn area in...
South Central Monterey County in central California...

* Until 1000 PM PST.

* At 747 PM PST, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges indicated
heavy rain falling over the Plaskett Burn Area. Between 2 and 5
inches of rain have fallen. The expected rainfall rate is 0.5 to
0.75 inches in 1 hour. Additional rainfall amounts of 0.5 to 1 inch
are possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or
expected to begin shortly. Excessive rainfall over the burn scar
will result in debris flow moving through the Alder, Plaskett, and
Prewitt Creeks. The debris flow can consist of rock, mud,
vegetation and other loose materials.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Heavy rain producing
flash flooding in and around the Plaskett Burn Area.

SOURCE...Radar and automated gauges.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of areas in and around the
Plaskett Burn Area.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
areas near CA Highway 1 mile marker 17 to mile marker 11 including
Los Burros Road.

Move away from recently burned areas. Life-threatening flooding of
creeks, and roads is likely. The heavy rains will likely trigger
rockslides, mudslides, and debris flows in steep terrain. Impacted
areas include locations along Los Burros Road, areas near Plaskett
Creek Campground and structures along the Alder, Plaskett, and
Prewitt Creeks.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

Stay away or be swept away. River banks and culverts can become
unstable and unsafe.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

properties.title: Flash Flood Warning
properties.rawText:
Flash Flood Warning issued November 18 at 7:46PM PST until November 18 at 10:00PM PST by NWS San Francisco CA

FFWMTR

The National Weather Service in San Francisco has extended the

* Flash Flood Warning for...
The Timber burn area in...
Western Monterey County in central California...

* Until 1000 PM PST.

* At 746 PM PST, CHP has reported an observed debris flow into NB
Highway One lanes in the vicinity of Big Sur Lodge and boulders in
the roadway at Hurricane Point. A car was reported stuck in the
debris flow near Big Sur. Doppler radar and automated rain gauges
indicated that heavy rain was falling over the Timber Burn Area.
Between 3 and 6 inches of rain have fallen. The expected rainfall
rate is 0.5 to 0.75 inches in 1 hour. Additional rainfall amounts
of 1 to 3 inches are possible in the warned area. Conditions remain
favorable for additional moderate to heavy rainfall due to
orographic lift as the main rainband exits the county. Flash
flooding is ongoing. Excessive rainfall over the burn scar will
result in debris flow moving through the Drainages within Lafler,
Castro and Graves Canyons, as well as drainages between Grimes and
Castro Canyons. The debris flow can consist of rock, mud,
vegetation and other loose materials.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Heavy rain producing
flash flooding in and around the Timber Burn Area.

SOURCE...Law enforcement reported.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of areas in and around the
Timber Burn Area.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
portions of CA Highway 1 and the Los Padres National Forecast from
Andrew Molera State Park to Partington Ridge including the town of
Big Sur.

At 5:43 PM PST CHP reported a debris flow across NB Highway 1 lanes
in the vicinity of Big Sur Lodge. One hour rain rates have crossed
0.7" with additional heavy rain expected this evening into tomorrow
as scattered showers with the potential for moderate to heavy rain
and thunderstorms. CHP additionally reported boulders in the NB lane
of Highway One at Hurricane Point at 6:11 PM local time. CHP reported
a car stuck in the debris flow at Big Sur.

Move away from recently burned areas. Life-threatening flooding of
creeks, and roads is likely. The heavy rains will likely trigger
rockslides, mudslides, and debris flows in steep terrain. Impacted
areas include locations along Highway 1 near mile marker 50 south of
Andrew Molera State Park to mile maker 38. Other areas impacted
include Pfeiffer Big Sur State Park Campground and Partington Ridge,
structures along the Big Sur River, Mule Creek Canyon, and adjacent
drainages and watershed outlets.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

properties.title: Flood Warning
properties.rawText:
Flood Warning issued November 18 at 10:02PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL

...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Cocoa 9w affecting Brevard County.

.Ongoing extreme rainfall over the headwaters of the St. Johns River
has caused the river near Cocoa to rise through Major Flood Stage.
Additional heavy rainfall over the next 48 hours will continue to
produce river rises, bringing record flood levels at this point
overnight Thursday into Friday morning. this weekend.

For the St. Johns River...including Cocoa 9w...Major flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast.
This is forecast to approach and surpass the flood of record.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Cocoa 9w.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 17.2 feet, Water enters homes along the St Johns River
in the Lake Poinsett area west of Cocoa, also low lying homes in
the Silver Pines subdivision in Rockledge and the Shakespeare Park
area of Cocoa. Providence Road area west of Cocoa becomes
impassable, cutting off access to homes in the Mullet Lane and Bass
Road area. Docks flooded and water in parking lot at Lone Cabbage
Fish Camp.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 9:15 PM EST Wednesday the stage was 17.4 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 15.8 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 9:15 PM EST Wednesday was 17.4 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to remain steady above flood
stage at 17.5 feet.
- Flood stage is 16.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued Thursday morning at 1115 AM EST.

properties.title: Flood Warning
properties.rawText:
Flood Warning issued November 18 at 8:19PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL

...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Astor affecting Lake and Volusia Counties.

.On the St Johns River at Astor, the river is forecast to continue to
rise through Moderate flood stage into next week due to strong
onshore flow causing a surge up the river as well as additional heavy
rainfall  expected across the basin.

For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 3.5 feet, Canals have overflowed into yards. Homes on
or near Wildhog, Bonnet and Snail roads become inaccessible with
several inches of water inside homes along the river and canals.
Docks at Astor Bridge marina and throughout Astor are completely
submerged. Bartram Rd and Holiday Circle are inaccessible with
yards completely submerged. Clair Street is inaccessible. Roads
flooded in South Moon Fish Camp, docks and yards at condominiums on
Juno Trail and water breaches the sea wall at Blair's Jungle Den.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:30 PM EST Wednesday the stage was 3.0 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 7:30 PM EST Wednesday was 3.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to 3.6 feet Sunday
evening. Additional rises are possible thereafter.
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued Thursday morning at 1100 AM EST.

FRONTAL PASSAGE WILL BRING THUNDERSTORMS TO THE COASTAL WATERS NOW

seas, dangerous lightning, heavy rainfall with reduced visibility,
and waterspouts..

properties.title: Flood Warning
properties.rawText:
Flood Warning issued November 19 at 8:48AM EST by NWS Melbourne FL

...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Above Lake Harney affecting Seminole County.

.Heavy rainfall over recent days has caused river levels on the St.
Johns near Geneva Above Lake Harney to rise through Moderate Flood
Stage. Additional heavy rainfall occurring across the basin is
forecast to allow the river to rise into Major Flood Stage tonight
into Friday morning, with continued rises through Major Flood Stage
into early next week.

For the St. Johns River...including Above Lake Harney...Major
flooding is forecast.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and major flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Above Lake Harney.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 10.8 feet, Water covers State Road 46 and it may
become impassable near Jungle Road and Prevatt Road. Standing water
on secondary roads near the river deepens to more than three feet
in some areas. Flooding becomes more significant to structures and
marinas from above Lake Harney to the Lake Jesup area.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:30 AM EST Thursday the stage was 9.7 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 6.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 7:30 AM EST Thursday was 9.7 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 12.3 feet
early Sunday afternoon.
- Flood stage is 8.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued this evening at 1100 PM EST.

properties.title: Flood Warning
properties.rawText:
Flood Warning issued November 19 at 8:38AM EST by NWS Melbourne FL

...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Cocoa 9w affecting Brevard County.

For the St. Johns River...including Cocoa 9w...Major flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast.
This passes the flood of record.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Cocoa 9w.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 17.2 feet, Water enters homes along the St Johns River
in the Lake Poinsett area west of Cocoa, also low lying homes in
the Silver Pines subdivision in Rockledge and the Shakespeare Park
area of Cocoa. Providence Road area west of Cocoa becomes
impassable, cutting off access to homes in the Mullet Lane and Bass
Road area. Docks flooded and water in parking lot at Lone Cabbage
Fish Camp.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:15 AM EST Thursday the stage was 18.1 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 15.8 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 8:15 AM EST Thursday was 18.1 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise and remain steady above
flood stage at 18.4 feet.
- Flood stage is 16.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

To escape rising water, take the shortest path to higher ground.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued this evening at 1100 PM EST.

Special Marine Warning issued November 19 at 5:17AM PST until November 19 at 7:00AM PST by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA

SMWLOX

The National Weather Service in Los Angeles/Oxnard has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
East Santa Barbara Channel from Pt. Conception to Pt. Mugu CA
including Santa Cruz Island...
Inner waters from Point Mugu to San Mateo Pt. CA including Santa
Catalina and Anacapa Islands...
Outer waters from Santa Cruz Island to San Clemente Island to 60 NM
offshore including San Nicolas and Santa Barbara Islands...

* Until 700 AM PST.

* At 517 AM PST, showers capable of producing strong wind gusts and
waterspouts were located along a line from near Rincon Point to 13
NM southwest of Anacapa Island, or along a line from 35 NM
northwest of Malibu to 23 NM east of Santa Rosa Island, moving east
at 15 knots.

HAZARD...Waterspouts possible and wind gusts to nearly 50 knots.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Waterspouts can create locally hazardous seas. Small craft
could be damaged in briefly higher winds and suddenly
higher waves.

* Locations impacted include...
Anacapa Island, Ventura Harbor, Point Mugu and Rincon Point.

Move to safe harbor until hazardous weather passes.

Move to safe harbor immediately as gusty winds and high waves are
expected.

properties.title: Flash Flood Warning
properties.rawText:
Flash Flood Warning issued November 19 at 7:35AM EST until November 19 at 9:45AM EST by NWS Melbourne FL

FFWMLB

The National Weather Service in Melbourne has extended the

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Central Brevard County in east central Florida...

* Until 945 AM EST.

* At 735 AM EST, the public reported thunderstorms producing heavy
rain across the warned area. Between 6 and 10 inches of rain have
fallen. Additional rainfall amounts of 2 to 4 inches are possible
in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...Public reported.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams,
urban areas, highways, streets and underpasses.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Melbourne, Titusville, Rockledge, Cocoa, Cocoa Beach, Satellite
Beach, Cape Canaveral, Merritt Island, Sharpes, Port Canaveral,
Port Saint John, Titusville Airport, Patrick Space Force Base,
Indian Harbour Beach, Jetty Park, Viera, Canaveral Groves, Suntree,
South Patrick Shores and Palm Shores.

Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...

Shores, Floridana Beach, Spessard Holland Park, Melbourne Airport
and Eau Gallie.

properties.title: Flood Warning
properties.rawText:
Flood Warning issued November 19 at 3:54AM EST by NWS Melbourne FL

...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Astor affecting Lake and Volusia Counties.

.On the St Johns River at Astor, the river is forecast to continue to
rise through Moderate flood stage into next week due to strong
onshore flow causing a surge up the river as well as additional heavy
rainfall expected across the basin.

For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 3.5 feet, Canals have overflowed into yards. Homes on
or near Wildhog, Bonnet and Snail roads become inaccessible with
several inches of water inside homes along the river and canals.
Docks at Astor Bridge marina and throughout Astor are completely
submerged. Bartram Rd and Holiday Circle are inaccessible with
yards completely submerged. Clair Street is inaccessible. Roads
flooded in South Moon Fish Camp, docks and yards at condominiums on
Juno Trail and water breaches the sea wall at Blair's Jungle Den.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 3:30 AM EST Thursday the stage was 3.1 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 3:30 AM EST Thursday was 3.1 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to 3.7 feet early Monday
morning. Additional rises are possible thereafter.
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued this afternoon at noon EST.

properties.title: Yellow warning · air quality warning
properties.rawText:
Elevated pollution levels are expected or occurring.

17th November 2026 - The Ministry of Environment and Parks in collaboration with the Northern Health Authority has issued an Air Quality Warning for Vanderhoof due to elevated coarse particulate matter.

Exposure to coarse particulate matter is particularly a concern for infants, older adults, individuals with chronic conditions (such as asthma, COPD, heart disease, and diabetes) or respiratory infections, and those who are pregnant.

Postpone or reduce strenuous outdoors activities until the warning has ended. Spend time indoors in a space with filtered air. Monitor your symptoms and seek prompt medical attention if needed.

Current conditions are expected to persist until weather conditions change and/or local emissions are reduced.

The next update will be on November 19, 2026 and posted to the province's Air Quality Warnings webpage.

Visit the provincial air quality data webpage for real-time observations.

Visit https://www.airhealth.ca for information on how to reduce your health risk and your personal contribution to pollution levels, as well as for current and forecast AQHI values.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada.

Issued by Environment Canada and the B.C. Ministry of Environment and Parks

properties.title: Severe Thunderstorm Warning
properties.rawText:
Severe Thunderstorm Warning issued November 19 at 1:38PM PST until November 19 at 2:30PM PST by NWS Hanford CA

SVRHNX

The National Weather Service in Hanford has issued a

* Severe Thunderstorm Warning for...
Northeastern Fresno County in central California...

* Until 230 PM PST.

* At 138 PM PST, severe thunderstorms were located along a line from
18 miles northeast of Clovis to 6 miles north of Sanger, or along a
line from 18 miles northeast of Clovis to 10 miles east of Clovis,
moving east at 25 mph.

HAZARD...60 mph wind gusts and quarter size hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Hail damage to vehicles is expected. Expect wind damage to
roofs, siding, and trees.

* Locations impacted include...
Trimmer Springs, Fancher Creek, Mountain Rest, Fence Meadow and
Shaver Lake.

Seek shelter inside a well-built structure and stay away from
windows. These storms are capable of producing damaging winds and
large hail.

Tornadoes can develop quickly from severe thunderstorms. Seek shelter
immediately in an interior room on the lowest floor of a well-built
structure.

Continuous cloud to ground lightning is occurring with these storms.
Lightning is one of nature's leading killers. Remember, if you can
hear thunder, you are close enough to be struck by lightning.

becomes inaccessible, with 1 to 2 feet water depth in numerous
homes on Wildhog, Possum, Bonnet and Snail roads. Roads along Blue
Creek are inaccessible with major flooding of homes on Otter,
Branch and Chestnut roads. Camp South Moon Road and Juno Trail are
inaccessible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:30 AM EST Thursday the stage was 3.2 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 8:30 AM EST Thursday was 3.2 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to 4.0 feet Monday
morning. Additional rises are possible thereafter.
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued this evening at 1100 PM EST.

properties.title: Yellow warning · air quality warning
properties.rawText:
Elevated pollution levels are expected or occurring.

The Ministry of Environment and Parks in collaboration with the Northern Health Authority has issued an Air Quality Warning for Smithers due to elevated coarse particulate matter. 

Exposure to coarse particulate matter is particularly a concern for infants, older adults, individuals with chronic conditions (such as asthma, COPD, heart disease, and diabetes) or respiratory infections, and those who are pregnant.

Postpone or reduce strenuous outdoor activities until the warning has ended. Spend time indoors in a space with filtered air. Monitor your symptoms and seek prompt medical attention if needed.

Current conditions are expected to persist until weather conditions change and/or local emissions are reduced.

The next update will be on November 19, 2026 and posted to the province’s Air Quality Warnings webpage.

Visit the provincial air quality data webpage for real-time observations.

Visit https://www.airhealth.ca for information on how to reduce your health risk and your personal contribution to pollution levels, as well as for current and forecast AQHI values.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada.

Issued by Environment Canada and the B.C. Ministry of Environment and Parks

properties.title: Yellow warning · blizzard warning
properties.rawText:
Blizzard conditions with poor visibility in blowing snow are expected.

Gusty northwesterly winds are giving near zero visibilities in blowing snow at Sanirajak this evening.

Visibilities will improve later this evening as winds subside.

Travel will likely be hazardous.

Blizzard warnings are issued when widespread poor visibility in blowing snow is expected.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to NUstorm@ec.gc.ca, call 1-800-239-0484 or post reports on social media using #NUStorm.

properties.title: Flash Flood Warning
properties.rawText:
Flash Flood Warning issued November 19 at 9:09PM EST until November 19 at 11:15PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL

FFWMLB

The National Weather Service in Melbourne has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Eastern Indian River County in east central Florida...

* Until 1115 PM EST.

* At 909 PM EST, emergency management reported flooding is occurring
on multiple roadways in Sebastian. Up to 1.5 inches of rain have
fallen. Additional rainfall amounts up to 1.5 inches are possible
in the warned area over the next hour and a half. Flash flooding is
already occurring.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by heavy rain.

SOURCE...Emergency management reported.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Sebastian, Vero Beach, Fellsmere, Indian River Shores, Wabasso,
Sebastian Highlands, Winter Beach, Gifford, Roseland, Vero Beach
South, Sebastian Inlet, Vero Lake Estates, Pointe West, Sebastian
Inlet State Park, Orchid, Vero Beach Airport, Wabasso Beach,
Disneys Vero Beach Resort and North Beach.

Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

properties.title: Flood Warning
properties.rawText:
Flood Warning issued November 19 at 8:46PM EST until November 20 at 6:00AM EST by NWS Melbourne FL

* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is occurring.

* WHERE...Southeastern Orange County in east central Florida...

* WHEN...Until 600 AM EST Friday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is imminent or occurring.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 844 PM EST, Florida 5-1-1 reported flooding along FL-520 in
the warned area. Flooding is already occurring.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...

KUWAIT FIR IS AVAILABLE FOR FLIGHTS ARR OR DEP WITHIN KUWAIT FIR 
SUBJECT TO PRIOR APPROVAL FROM KUWAIT DGCA AIR TRANSPORT DEPARTMENT. 
 
OVERFLIGHT TFC OPERATING BTN BAHRAIN FIR ( OBBB ) 
AND BAGHDAD FIR ( ORBB ) VIA KUWAIT FIR ( OKAC ) 
IS PERMITTED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS VIA PUBLISHED ATS ROUTES 
FL 280 AND ABOVE SUBJECT TO PRIOR APPROVAL FROM KUWAIT DGCA AIR 
TRANSPORT DEPARTMENT, FLOW CONTROL MEASURES AND ATC CLEARANCE. 
 
ALL OTHER OVERFLIGHT OPERATIONS THROUGH KUWAIT FIR NOT PERMITTED. 
 
FLIGHTS DEPARTING FROM OR ARRIVING AT AIRPORTS WITHIN KUWAIT FIR 
TO/FROM BAGHDAD FIR ( ORBB ) ARE NOT PERMITTED. 
 
 
DEPARTING TFC FROM AIRPORTS WITHIN KUWAIT FIR 
SHALL USE THE FOLLOWING ROUTING : 
 
A.TFC DESTINED TO AIRPORTS WITHIN OBBB FIR OR OVERFLYING 
 OBBB FIR FOR DESTINATIONS OUTSIDE OBBB FIR SHALL FILE IN ACCORDANCE 
WITH THE NORMAL ROUTING ARRANGEMENTS BETWEEN OKAC AND OBBB FIRS AS 
APPLICABLE TO DESTINATION. 
 
B.TFC DESTINED TO AIRPORTS WITHEN JEDDAH FIR ( OEJD ) OR OVERFLYING 
JEDDAH FIR SHALL FILE VIA NIDAP L550 OR DEKOB P517 OR KATOD G667 OR 
ASVIR H741 AS APPROPRIATE TO DESTINATION. 
 
ARRIVING TFC AIRPORTS END PART 1 OF 2

B.TFC ARRIVING FROM OEJD FIR SHALL FILE VIA KUNRU P891 OR SOROR A788 
OR H741 ASVIR. 
 
OPERATORS SHALL CARRY SUFFICIENT FUEL TO ACCOMMODATE POSSIBLE DELAYS

properties.title: Flood Warning
properties.rawText:
Flood Warning issued November 20 at 5:21AM EST by NWS Melbourne FL

...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Astor affecting Volusia and Lake Counties.

.The St Johns River at Astor is forecast to continue to rise through
Moderate Flood Stage, reaching Major Flood Stage early next week due
to heavy rainfall working its way through the basin in combination
with strong north-northeast flow.

For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Major flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and major flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 4.0 feet, Major flooding occurs with water entering
many structures on canals and along the river. Long duration
flooding will occur, with levels taking weeks to months to return
below flood stage. Water rescues will be necessary. River Road
becomes inaccessible, with 1 to 2 feet water depth in numerous
homes on Wildhog, Possum, Bonnet and Snail roads. Roads along Blue
Creek are inaccessible with major flooding of homes on Otter,
Branch and Chestnut roads. Camp South Moon Road and Juno Trail are
inaccessible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 4:30 AM EST Friday the stage was 3.6 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 4:30 AM EST Friday was 3.6 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to 4.0 feet Tuesday
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued this morning at 1100 AM EST.

properties.title: Flood Warning
properties.rawText:
Flood Warning issued November 20 at 3:10AM EST by NWS Melbourne FL

...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Cocoa 9w affecting Brevard County.

.Extreme rainfall over the headwaters of the St. Johns River has
caused the river near Cocoa to rise through Major Flood Stage, well
above its previous record flood stage. Any additional heavy rainfall
over the next 48 hours will continue to produce river rises above
record flood levels through late week and into this weekend.

For the St. Johns River...including Cocoa 9w...Major flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast.
This approaches the flood of record.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Cocoa 9w.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 17.2 feet, Water enters homes along the St Johns River
in the Lake Poinsett area west of Cocoa, also low lying homes in
the Silver Pines subdivision in Rockledge and the Shakespeare Park
area of Cocoa. Providence Road area west of Cocoa becomes
impassable, cutting off access to homes in the Mullet Lane and Bass
Road area. Docks flooded and water in parking lot at Lone Cabbage
Fish Camp.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 2:15 AM EST Friday the stage was 18.6 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 15.8 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 2:15 AM EST Friday was 18.6 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to remain steady within Major
Flood Stage, cresting at 18.7 feet.
- Flood stage is 16.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

To escape rising water, take the shortest path to higher ground.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued this afternoon at noon EST.

properties.title: Flash Flood Warning
properties.rawText:
Flash Flood Warning issued November 20 at 2:58AM EST until November 20 at 6:00AM EST by NWS Melbourne FL

FFWMLB

The National Weather Service in Melbourne has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Central Brevard County in east central Florida...

* Until 600 AM EST.

* At 258 AM EST, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain across the warned
area. Up to 1.5 and 2.5 inches of rain have fallen over the past
few hours, on top of areas that have already received very heavy
rainfall over the past 24 hours. Additional rainfall amounts of 1
to 2 inches are possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is
ongoing or expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by heavy rain.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Titusville, Rockledge, Cocoa, Cocoa Beach, Satellite Beach, Cape
Canaveral, Sharpes, Port Saint John, Port Canaveral, Merritt
Island, Titusville Airport, Patrick Space Force Base, Jetty Park,
Canaveral Groves, Viera, South Patrick Shores, Palm Shores,
Bellwood and Canaveral Acres.

Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

properties.title: Flood Warning
properties.rawText:
Flood Warning issued November 19 at 11:40PM EST until November 20 at 7:55PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL

...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

Little Wekiva River near Altamonte Springs 2n affecting Seminole
County.

.The Little Wekiva River near Altamonte Springs continues to
gradually rise as rainfall works through the basin. Additional heavy
rainfall with amounts of 2 to 4 inches will be possible through
tomorrow, which could lead to additional rises. The river is forecast
to reach Minor Flood Stage Friday morning and will continue in flood
stage through Friday evening.

For the Little Wekiva...including Altamonte Springs 2n...Minor
flooding is forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Little Wekiva River near Altamonte Springs 2n.

* WHEN...From Friday morning to Friday evening.

* IMPACTS...At 28.5 feet, Minor flooding near the river in the
Altamonte Springs area.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 10:30 PM EST Thursday the stage was 27.1 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 27.5 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage Friday
morning, cresting at 28.7 feet late Friday morning into Friday
afternoon. It will then fall below flood stage tomorrow evening.
Additional rises due to heavy rainfall cannot be ruled out.
- Flood stage is 28.5 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued Friday afternoon at 1215 PM EST.

properties.title: Yellow advisory · fog advisory
properties.rawText:
Near-zero visibility in fog is expected.

Dense patchy fog has reduced visibility over parts of southern Manitoba including the Red River Valley.

The fog may lift in some areas today but is expected to persist through out the day.

Travel will likely be hazardous in some locations.

Be prepared for areas of near-zero visibility and allow extra time to reach your destination. If driving, turn on your lights, slow down and maintain a safe following distance.

Fog advisories are issued when widespread poor visibility in fog is expected.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to MBstorm@ec.gc.ca, call 1-800-239-0484 or post reports on social media using #MBStorm.

properties.title: Yellow warning · air quality warning
properties.rawText:
Elevated pollution levels are expected or occurring.

The Ministry of Environment and Parks in collaboration with the Northern Health Authority has issued an Air Quality Warning for Smithers due to elevated coarse particulate matter. 

Exposure to coarse particulate matter is particularly a concern for infants, older adults, individuals with chronic conditions (such as asthma, COPD, heart disease, and diabetes) or respiratory infections, and those who are pregnant.

Postpone or reduce strenuous outdoor activities until the warning has ended. Spend time indoors in a space with filtered air. Monitor your symptoms and seek prompt medical attention if needed.

Current conditions are expected to persist until weather conditions change and/or local emissions are reduced.

The next update will be on November 20, 2026 and posted to the province’s Air Quality Warnings webpage.

Visit the provincial air quality data webpage for real-time observations.

Visit https://www.airhealth.ca for information on how to reduce your health risk and your personal contribution to pollution levels, as well as for current and forecast AQHI values.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada.

Issued by Environment Canada and the B.C. Ministry of Environment and Parks

properties.title: Special Marine Warning
properties.rawText:
Special Marine Warning issued November 20 at 1:34PM EST until November 20 at 2:30PM EST by NWS Jacksonville FL

SMWJAX

The National Weather Service in Jacksonville has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
Waters from Fernandina Beach to St. Augustine FL from 20 to 60
NM...
Waters from St. Augustine to Flagler Beach FL from 20 to 60 NM...

* Until 230 PM EST.

* At 134 PM EST, a severe thunderstorm capable of producing
waterspouts was located 38 nm east of Daytona Beach Shores, or 39
nm east of South Daytona, moving north at 20 knots.

HAZARD...Waterspouts and wind gusts to 45 knots.

SOURCE...Radar.

IMPACT...Waterspouts can easily overturn boats and create locally
hazardous seas. Small craft could be damaged in briefly
higher winds and suddenly higher waves.

* The severe thunderstorm will remain over mainly open waters.

Move to safe harbor immediately as gusty winds and high waves are
expected. If your vessel is caught offshore, immediately secure for
heavy weather. Ensure all crew members are wearing USCG approved Type
I life jackets and nonessential crew are below decks. Deploy jack
lines and harnesses if available. Check life saving equipment,
including batteries on handheld radios, for readiness.

Thunderstorms can produce sudden waterspouts. Waterspouts can easily
overturn boats and create locally hazardous seas. Seek safe harbor
immediately. If your vessel is caught offshore, immediately secure
for heavy weather. Ensure all crew members are wearing USCG approved
Type I life jackets and nonessential crew are below decks. Deploy
jack lines and harnesses if available. Check life saving equipment,
including batteries on handheld radios, for readiness.
