properties.title: Flood Warning
properties.rawText:
Flood Warning issued November 20 at 9:20AM EST by NWS Melbourne FL

...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Astor affecting Lake and Volusia Counties.

.The St Johns River at Astor is forecast to continue to rise through
Moderate Flood Stage, reaching Major Flood Stage early next week due
to heavy rainfall working its way through the basin in combination
with strong north-northeast flow.

For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Major flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and major flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 4.0 feet, Major flooding occurs with water entering
many structures on canals and along the river. Long duration
flooding will occur, with levels taking weeks to months to return
below flood stage. Water rescues will be necessary. River Road
becomes inaccessible, with 1 to 2 feet water depth in numerous
homes on Wildhog, Possum, and Bonnet roads. Roads along Blue Creek
are inaccessible with major flooding of homes on Otter, Branch and
Chestnut roads. Camp South Moon Road and Juno Trail are
inaccessible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:30 AM EST Friday the stage was 3.7 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 8:30 AM EST Friday was 3.7 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to remain steady above flood
stage at 3.8 feet.
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued this evening at 1100 PM EST.

properties.title: Flood Warning
properties.rawText:

...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Cocoa 9w affecting Brevard County.

.Extreme rainfall over the headwaters of the St. Johns River has
caused the river near Cocoa to rise through Major Flood Stage, well
above its previous record flood stage. The river level will continue
a slow rise through tonight and is expected to become steady this
weekend into early next week.

For the St. Johns River...including Cocoa 9w, Above Lake Harney,
Sanford, Deland, Astor...Major flooding is forecast.

* WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast.
This will set an all time flood of record.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Cocoa 9w.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 17.2 feet, Water enters homes along the St Johns River
in the Lake Poinsett area west of Cocoa, also low lying homes in
the Silver Pines subdivision in Rockledge and the Shakespeare Park
area of Cocoa. Providence Road area west of Cocoa becomes
impassable, cutting off access to homes in the Mullet Lane and Bass
Road area. Docks flooded and water in parking lot at Lone Cabbage
Fish Camp.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...

- Bankfull stage is 15.8 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 8:15 AM EST Friday was 18.7 feet.

Saturday and remain steady near that level into early next week.

properties.title: special weather statement
properties.rawText:
Snowfall expected early this weekend.

What:
Snow with total amounts of 5 to 10 cm.
Reduced visibility in heavy snow.

When:
Beginning this evening and ending Saturday afternoon.

Additional information:
A low pressure system tracking northeast across the region will bring a wintery mix of precipitation which may include heavy snowfall to some areas.

Allow extra time for travel. Prepare for possible disruptions to transportation, services and utilities.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to ONstorm@ec.gc.ca or post reports on social media using #ONStorm.

properties.title: Yellow advisory · blowing snow advisory
properties.rawText:
WHAT: 
POOR VISIBILITY IN BLOWING SNOW. 

WHEN: 
LATE THIS AFTERNOON.

WHERE: 
DEMPSTER HIGHWAY NEAR THE RICHARDSON MOUNTAINS. 

ADDITIONAL INFORMATION: 
A LOW PRESSURE SYSTEM OVER THE BEAUFORT SEA WILL GENERATE STRONG WINDS ACROSS THE RICHARDSON MOUNTAINS. 

SOUTHWESTERLY TO WESTERLY WINDS WITH GUSTS TO 60 KM/H WILL RESULT IN POOR VISIBILITY IN BLOWING SNOW LATE THIS AFTERNOON. WINDS SHOULD EASE OVERNIGHT.

Travel will likely be hazardous. Road closures are possible.

If driving, turn on your lights, slow down and maintain a safe following distance.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to YTstorm@ec.gc.ca or post reports on social media using #YTStorm.

properties.rawText:
Gale Warning issued November 20 at 7:16PM EST until November 21 at 7:00AM EST by NWS Tallahassee FL

* WHAT...Northeast winds 20 to 30 kt with gusts up to 35 kt.

* WHERE...Nearshore Gulf waters from the Ochlockonee River to
the Suwannee River out 20 nautical miles.

* WHEN...Until 7 AM EST Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Strong winds will cause hazardous seas which could
capsize or damage vessels and reduce visibility.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Coastal observations and VAD wind profiles
this evening have been showing strong gradient winds in the
warning area with reports of frequent gale-force gusts aided by
a nearby area of low pressure.

Mariners should alter plans to avoid these hazardous conditions.
Remain in port, seek safe harbor, alter course, and/or secure the
vessel for severe conditions.

Marine Weather Statement issued November 20 at 7:44PM AST by NWS San Juan PR

A Marine Weather Statement has been issued for the following areas...
Atlantic Waters of Puerto Rico and USVI from 10 NM to 19.5N...
Coastal Waters of Northern Puerto Rico out 10 NM...

* At 744 PM AST, Doppler radar indicated a strong thunderstorm,
capable of producing winds to around 30 knots. The strong
thunderstorm was off to the northwest at around 10 nautical miles
of Aguadilla, moving northwest at 5 knots.

Locations impacted include...
Mainly open waters of Atlantic Waters of Puerto Rico and USVI from
10 NM to 19.5N and Coastal Waters of Northern Puerto Rico out 10
NM.

Report severe weather to the Coast Guard or nearest law enforcement
agency. They will relay your report to the National Weather Service
office.

Mariners can expect gusty winds to around 30 knots, locally higher
waves, and lightning strikes. Boaters should seek safe harbor
immediately until this storm passes.

...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Deland affecting Volusia and Lake Counties.

.Heavy rainfall has maintained a steady climb into Moderate Flood
Stage on the St Johns River at Deland, with river levels forecast to
continue climbing through this weekend. The river is anticipated to
reach Major Flood Stage on Saturday.

For the St. Johns River...including Deland...Major flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and major flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Deland.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 5.3 feet, Major flooding occurs to many structures and
marinas along the river and in the Hontoon Island area.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1:30 PM EST Friday the stage was 4.9 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 3.5 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 1:30 PM EST Friday was 4.9 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to 6.0 feet Tuesday
evening. Additional rises are possible thereafter. This
approaches the flood of record which is 6.3 feet.
- Flood stage is 4.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

properties.title: Flood Warning
properties.rawText:
Flood Warning issued November 20 at 9:15PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL

...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Deland affecting Volusia and Lake Counties.

.Heavy rainfall has maintained a steady climb into Moderate Flood
Stage on the St Johns River at Deland, with river levels forecast to
continue climbing through next week. The river is anticipated to
reach Major Flood Stage this weekend, with additional rises
thereafter.

For the St. Johns River...including Deland...Major flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and major flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Deland.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 5.3 feet, Major flooding occurs to many structures and
marinas along the river and in the Hontoon Island area.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:30 PM EST Friday the stage was 5.0 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 3.5 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 8:30 PM EST Friday was 5.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to 6.0 feet early next
week. Additional rises are possible thereafter.
- Flood stage is 4.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued Saturday afternoon at noon EST.

Special Marine Warning issued November 21 at 10:29AM EST until November 21 at 11:00AM EST by NWS Miami FL

SMWMFL

The National Weather Service in Miami has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
Coastal waters from East Cape Sable to Chokoloskee FL out 20 NM...

* Until 1100 AM EST.

* At 1029 AM EST, a severe thunderstorm capable of producing
waterspouts was located over Shark Point, moving east at 15 knots.

HAZARD...Waterspouts, wind gusts to nearly 50 knots, and small
hail.

SOURCE...Radar.

IMPACT...Waterspouts can easily overturn boats and create locally
hazardous seas. Small craft could be damaged in briefly
higher winds and suddenly higher waves.

* Locations impacted include...
Shark Point, Whitewater Bay, and Northwest Cape Sable.

Move to safe harbor until hazardous weather passes.

Report severe weather to the Coast Guard or the National Weather
Service. You can also share your report with NWS Miami on Facebook
and Twitter.

properties.title: Flood Warning
properties.rawText:
Flood Warning issued November 21 at 8:24AM EST by NWS Melbourne FL

...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Astor affecting Volusia and Lake Counties.

.Heavy rainfall working its way through the basin, in combination
with strong north-northeast flow, has caused river levels on The St
Johns River at Astor to rise into Major Flood Stage. Continued rises
through Major Flood Stage are forecast through mid next week.

For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Major flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 4.0 feet, Major flooding occurs with water entering
many structures on canals and along the river. Long duration
flooding will occur, with levels taking weeks to months to return
below flood stage. Water rescues will be necessary. River Road
becomes inaccessible, with 1 to 2 feet water depth in numerous
homes on Wildhog, Possum, and Bonnet roads. Roads along Blue Creek
are inaccessible with major flooding of homes on Otter, Branch and
Chestnut roads. Camp South Moon Road and Juno Trail are
inaccessible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:30 AM EST Saturday the stage was 4.0 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 7:30 AM EST Saturday was 4.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to remain steady above flood
stage at 4.0 feet.
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued this evening at 1100 PM EST.

Gale Warning issued November 21 at 12:38AM PST until November 21 at 4:00PM PST by NWS Seattle WA

* WHAT...For the Gale Warning, southeast winds 25 to 35 kt. For
the Small Craft Advisory, southeast winds 20 to 30 kt and seas 8
to 12 ft.

* WHERE...Coastal Waters From Cape Flattery To James Island 10
To 60 Nm.

* WHEN...For the Gale Warning, until 4 PM PST this afternoon.
For the Small Craft Advisory, from 4 PM this afternoon to 4 AM
PST Sunday.

* IMPACTS...Strong winds will cause hazardous seas which could
capsize or damage vessels and reduce visibility.

A Gale Warning means winds of 34 to 47 knots are imminent or
occurring. Operating a vessel in gale conditions requires
experience and properly equipped vessels. It is highly
recommended that mariners without the proper experience seek safe
harbor prior to the onset of gale conditions.

properties.rawText:
Marine Weather Statement issued November 21 at 2:08AM CST by NWS Houston/Galveston TX

Areas of dense fog are forming in inland areas near Matagorda Bay.
It is likely that patchy dense fog is already impacting portions
of the upper bay. We cannot rule out the fog increasing in
coverage in portions of the bay, possibly warranting a Marine
Dense Fog Advisory. Any fog should break by mid morning.

* WHAT...For the Gale Warning, south winds 25 to 35 kt with gusts
up to 40 kt and very steep seas of 8 to 12 ft at 8 to 9 seconds
expected. For the Small Craft Advisory, southwest winds 15 to
25 kt with gusts up to 30 kt and seas 12 to 17 ft between 10 and
14 seconds expected.

* WHERE...All the area.

* WHEN...For the Gale Warning, until 9 AM PST Saturday. For the
Small Craft Advisory, from 9 AM Saturday to 4 AM PST Monday.

* IMPACTS...Strong winds and very steep seas could capsize or
damage vessels. Low visibility conditions are expected.

Mariners should alter plans to avoid strong winds and very steep
seas. Remain in port, seek safe harbor, alter course, and/or
secure the vessel for severe conditions.

properties.title: special weather statement
properties.rawText:
Heavy snowfall expected Sunday.

What:
Snow with total amounts of 10 to 20 cm.
Reduced visibility in heavy snow.

When:
Beginning Sunday morning and ending Sunday evening.

Additional information:
A low pressure system tracking northeast across the region will bring heavy snow. A snowfall warning may be issued as the event approaches. 

Allow extra time for travel. Prepare for possible disruptions to transportation, services and utilities.
